Vu A
Kære Caroline S,
Tusind tak for dine utroligt generøse og varme ord om din oplevelse hos Noir. Dining in the Dark. At læse, at du mener stedet er Michelin-stjerne værdigt, er en kompliment af den slags, som hele vores team vil blive dybt rørt og stolte over.
Vi er meget glade for at høre, at både maden, servicen og formålet bag oplevelsen gjorde indtryk på dig. Hos Noir forsøger vi at skabe noget mere end blot en middag – et øjeblik hvor sanserne vågner på en ny måde, hvor smag og teksturer træder frem i mørket, og hvor man samtidig får et lille indblik i en verden, hvor synet ikke er den primære guide.
Dine ord om det smukke formål betyder særligt meget for os. Vores synshæmmede team er hjertet i Noir, og det er deres professionalisme, ro og varme, der gør oplevelsen mulig hver eneste aften. At du har bemærket og værdsat dette, betyder virkelig meget for os alle.
Vi er også meget glade for, at maden gjorde så stærkt et indtryk. Vores køkkenteam arbejder med stor omhu for at skabe retter, hvor smag, duft og tekstur kan stå helt i centrum, når synet træder i baggrunden.
Endnu en gang tak fordi du delte din oplevelse så smukt. Vi håber, at mindet om aftenen hos Noir vil blive hos dig længe – og vi vil være meget glade for at byde dig velkommen igen en dag til endnu en rejse gennem sanserne.
Med venlig hilsen,

BEST NIGHT.
We have been to other restaurants like Noir, and always enjoyed trying to guess what we were eating. Mr T and I love food, love to eat, and usually do a good job of working out what we were eating.
This is a different story.
I think we may have got 2 or 3 things correct.
We entered and got a cocktail and a game to train us at finding food. This was fun!
I went really well, and sat there laughing and laughing at Mr T, who eventually had to cheat to finalise the task.
We were then shown to our table by our wait staff. She was lovely. Lead us quietly and efficiently to our table. She filled up our wine glasses, and continued to all night. We were absolutely amazed at her efficiency of knowing how much was in the glass, and how much more to add.
AMAZING.

The food was interesting and we were surprised at some of the things we were served.
Don't worry, you are not eating bugs and things like that. Anyone can go here without being scared.

The food was tasty, but as mentioned, we struggled picking the protein, sauces, etc.

A fabulous night finished up by being shown photos and descriptions of your food.
I would highly recommend anyone going to Noir.

Fabulous.

Overall, this was a fantastic experience. Our server, Ms. Phuong was phenomenal and really made our experience great. She was kind, an excellent server, and very helpful. She was on a par with many of the most excellent fully sighted servers we have had at higher end restaurants. Dining in the dark was an eye-opening experience, if you will excuse the expression, as to the challenges of the sight impaired. Spending an hour of our lives dining without our sight was truly enlightening as to only one of the many challenges the sight impaired are faced with every day. We are blessed to return to a world where we are able to eat and see what we are eating, while others are not. We hope we remember this experience long after it is over. The food was rich in variety and provided an interesting array of flavors and textures. One note I would make is that if you have a food allergy, make sure the staff is aware of exactly what you are allergic to and be very clear about it. I have a minor food allergy and reported it to the staff; two of the staff members incorrectly identified my food allergen and had it been a worse allergy, I would have been more concerned. This is a negligible problem as clear and direct communication could easily solve it. We highly recommend this experience for anyone willing to step outside of their comfort zone and experience something impactful.

Dinner at Noir restaurant with friends
Jul 2023 • Friends
Tonight we decided to try a completely new experience by dining at Noir restaurant. 
This restaurant is about using all but one of your sensors. We first started with a blind fold and had to complete a puzzle ( putting the correct block into the correctly shaped spot, like the traditional kid’s puzzle). Thanks to one of my friends for moving everyone’s pieces around to really make it a challenge. 
Then like a Congo line we went into a completely black room each being expertly seated one at a time before a selection of dishes was served. I am sure they looked amazing. We had a selection of 4 entrees, 4 mains and 3 desserts. I never knew how different it was to eat without first sampling food with your eyes,(there may have been a few dropped morsels for the cleaners to find later)!
The best part about the restaurant is that all the wait staff are blind and the bar staff are deaf and can not speak. What a great restaurant to experience and fabulous opportunities for the staff.
Upon completion of our meal we were shown exactly what we were eating. My favourite may have been the smoked goose, something that I would not have ordered from a menu.

Such a memorable and fun experience - a must-try!
Mar 2023
The concept is fascinating, a restaurant where you eat in total darkness. But, importantly, it’s also both a fun experience and has really good food! When you arrive, you practice the kind of skill you’ll need during the meal by trying to solve a children’s block puzzle while blindfolded. Much harder than you’d think! When you’re ready to eat, you’re led into the (completely black) dining area by the wait staff (who are all blind). Each course is a selection of 3-4 small dishes which are a complete surprise. You have to use your other senses to try to figure out what it is and how to get the food to your mouth. And not being able to see what you’re eating makes the experience so different! We informed them about my wife’s celiac disease and they were able to modify her dishes accordingly to avoid gluten and made sure they were free from cross-contamination.
After the meal, a member of the staff shows you photos of the food you were served, and it was so much fun to see what you were able to figure out in the dark. It gave me so much more of an appreciation for how much we rely on sight when eating, both in terms of taste and in terms of navigating all of the utensils and glasses and dishes! And it’s fantastic that this restaurant is a great way for servers who are impaired to be uniquely qualified for the job!

Amazing Experience
Sep 2022
On our Vietnam holiday we wanted to do something unique and amazing for my daughter’s birthday so we made a reservation at Noir.
Upon arrival we were greeted with a welcome drink and our hostess explained the concept of the dining experience. We were blindfolded and encouraged to play a couple of games to enhance our senses of touch.

We ordered our cocktails and drinks to go with our East meets west Mystery tasting menu and then followed a staffer with a hand to shoulder chain through a door in to total darkness. This was quite an experience in complete darkness, we had no idea where other diners were seated, how large the restaurant was, or the location of our table. For a few short hours we lived like visually impaired people and learned that sight is a precious gift.
Our waiter was visually impaired but for us he was the real star of the evening, always attentive, friendly and gave us clear instructions to help us have a great and memorable experience.

The food was excellent with each course outdoing the other. The great part was that you could ask for seconds if you liked a particular dish and they will serve it complimentary.
We discussed the different dishes and got most of them wrong after they were revealed at the end of the meal.

I cannot recommend this highly enough

Dear Ms Franziska and friends, 

My name is Vũ Anh Tú, founder/owner of Noir. Dining in the Dark. 

Firstly, please accept my sincerest apology for the uncomfortable feeling that you have been through due to this unexpected situation. 

Secondly, I am writing to further understand and explain the situation that has happened with your table last night in Noir., but before that I have to say, I had a conversation with Ms Ngoc who booked the table and placed the order on behalf of your group. And she agreed with me there must be a miscommunication from both sides. 
• Your group is expecting Noir. Dining in the Dark is a full-on vegetarian restaurant, but actually one of our three menus is vegetarian, the other two menus have meat and fish dishes. We do have a separate vegetarian restaurant, Du Du Xanh, located in the same lane. Maybe you mixed the two restaurants up?
• Your order menu is Premium menu (14 dishes) which is non-vegetarian option, please have a look in attached menu or this link http://www.noirdininginthedark.com/qr/ 
• The waiter who took your order repeated the order and asked if anyone of have any food allergy. And he got the confirmation from your group that there are no requests. 
• In the lounge area, there are few speaking staffs (one manager, one bartender/cashier and one waiter who took your order), the rest of the team are deaf and hearing-impairment. Perhaps not sure that you spoke to any of them about your request? 
• In our restaurant, we receive almost everyday many similar requests regarding dietary restrictions and food allergies, including severe (deadly) allergies, which always come to us with utmost fully attention and we have many different ways of cross check to ensure the guests feel safe and enjoy the experience. In other words we do take requests very seriously. 
• For your situation, there is no reason for us not to fulfill your request. On other side, we always fully aware, as human person mistake might take place, but we wonder if anyone in your group notice having the wrong menu then please do let us know straightaway so we can fix it immediately.

A special experience for a special day
May 2021
Today is my girlfriend’s birthday and we chose Noir for this special day. And it was more than perfect.
- Everything was so smooth from the booking progress. I booked 1 day before the event and got confirmation right away with very clear detail on dress code, parking place... When I called for reservation and said that it was the birthday, they ask me if I want to have flowers and cake (I said yes for flower, no for cake, and ask for a small card). They were very caring and supportive. Especially, very clear and transparent with me about the extra fee.
- If you go by car, they will suggest you in the confirmation email to park at either a park or the MB tower. But it seems like the guard in MB tower doesn’t know what Noir is and if we can park there so I would recommend you to go parking at the park.
- We were welcomed by a warm and friendly host with amazing free drinks and a very practical game to get used to the dark. Then, we were hosted by a very professional guide (whom I later known was blind).
- The course was amazing with the great support from our guide. After appetizers, the staffs come and sing a surprise happy birthday song to my girl, which was a super nice experience (being sung happy birthday in the dark to avoid eye contact is always one of her dream).
- At the end of the amazing meal, we were given a special gifts from the staffs - I will keep it as a secret for you to explore but believe me it was super nice and special. 
- After that, the staff guide us to the light and while we were waiting at the sofa, Noir surprised us again with the Happy Birthday song again, but this time is with hand signals (video attached below). They also gave us the flower and card (which I have ordered before but it was beyond my expectation) and a tiramisu cake with candle (this is WOW). And the extra fee for it is super reasonable (Noir only charge me 1xx.000). We were so full at that time so we decided to pack the cake home. The host is very sweet and walked us out. I could not ask for more. 
- We totally love the place, the experience and the vision that Noir has: in some places, the blind may need the support from other, but in Noir, other needs to be assisted by the blind. We had a lot of realization and reflection during the meal. The taste and conversation was way much better comparing to other experiences. 
Definitely recommend this place and go here again.

reviews.review_text:

A different kind of experience
Feb 2020
I wanted to try this concept since it came about over a decade ago but there is no dining in the dark resto in my country. So when this opportunity came, I decided to also bring my family to have a taste of this unique experience. And we were not disappointed.

From the time of my reservation, Noir already gave a very good impression. They responded promptly to my emails and accommodated my dietary requests without question. When we arrived, we were greeted warmly and served some cold drinks (I only wish that that the glass was not just half-full since we were so thirsty at that time). We also played a little game which gave us a feel of how it is to work with our hands without our sight to guide us. 

My family, which included my 80 year old mother and 87 year old father, was not prepared for what is in store for them since I didn't tell them anything. Nevertheless, they enjoyed every bit of the challenge (it wasn't easy scooping food and bringing it to your mouth when it is pitch black). There were lots of conversations and laughter since we didn't have our mobile phones to distract us. It was really good for family bonding.

Food was also great. My son, who doesn't eat mushrooms, finished his bowl of salad which was mainly composed of well...mushrooms. In normal days, maybe we would have skipped some of the ingredients which we usually don't like or are not familiar with but since we can't see anything, we simply ate everything with gusto.

Price was a little bit high and it doesn't include drinks but if it is a different kind of experience that you are after, it was all worth it.

reviews.review_title: Review at Noir Dining In The Dark
reviews.review_text:
Karen T
Auckland Central, New Zealand99 contributions
2
Unforgettable dining experience
Jan 2020
My son and partner live in Saigon and said they wanted us to have a special Date Night while in Ho Chi Minh. They booked us into a restaurant, booked the 'Grab' and off we went having no idea where we were going. 
At around 4.30 our Grab cab drove us through rush hour... or in Saigon's case crazier than normal with even more toot toot, brake slamming, cheeky motorcyclist, buses and other cars trying to swerve into your space -but it always seems to be perfectly orchestrated.
At 5.30 we arrived to our restaurant in a quiet alleyway off a busy main road in District One. We were given complimentary drinks... but why asked to do a puzzle blindfolded?
We were asked to select our menu, introduced to our host and were then led into various shades of light until our host (blind) told me to put my hand on his shoulder and in turn my husband put his hand on mine and it was a case of the blind leading the blind to our table, where we found our seats for a dining experience where we sat and ate in Noir (pitch blackness).
But what an experience it was! Try clinking wine glasses when you can't see the person in front of you. We had no idea what we were eating, but lots of conversation and guessing... the food was sensational - and it very soon became quite obvious why we were asked to do a puzzle blind folded! What can I say - it was the most humbling but beautiful experience. Afterwards we were taken through our menu and wines and told about how this restaurant gives blind and deaf people work opportunities which are hard to come by in Vietnam.
But wait - there's more
Three months ago the managers of Noir opened a spa and as we had arrived at the restaurant a little early we were given the opportunity to check it out..... well what happened as a result is that we booked for a Vietnamese bath and foot massage after our meal - it really was the 'icing on the cake' Well to be honest that foot massage was bliss - I hope I didn't snore too loudly - it was absolutely glorious!

Exceeded expectations
Dec 2019
Me and my partner went after a recommendation from a friend. I was quite sceptical, thinking this would be a posh, expensive gimmick. However, I was very pleasantly surprised. No doubt, this place is fancy for Vietnam and as a young backpacker, it was a very different experience with a different crowd. While it is expensive for Vietnam standards (understandably so), it is far cheaper (by $100AUD at least) than the same experience in Australia.

Firstly, all staff speak impeccable English, making communication very easy. 
There is a complimentary drink upon arrival, and a small sensory deprivation puzzle, which gave us an insight into life without sight. While this could seem like a gimmick, the staff seemed genuinely interested in showing us what life without one of our senses could be, and it didn't feel gimmicky at all. 

The food itself was delicious, the waiter was fantastic and we had great fun trying to guess all the ingredients. The drinks were excellent. 

I would highly recommend taking the earliest session available. We did so because we were hungry, but the benefit was that we were alone in the pitch black. reviews.review_text:
Jeffrey B
30 contributions

It's no fun being blind
Nov 2019
This is a tricky review to write, because on the one hand (and really most importantly) Noir is a fantastic way to support the visually and audibly impaired, and that truly is an innovative and commendable way to support these communities. Eating here is as much, if not more, of a philosophical experience than a gastronomical one, because you are obviously forced to appreciate a world which you take for granted. But if that's what you want to feel, it is just as easily achieved by blindfolding yourself during any meal. So, on the flip side, Noir is really little more than a novelty restaurant at its essence. The food was delicious, but boy, did I want to see it. I felt I was in a reality game show or on partaking in children's class activity, guessing at what the flavors were, surprised as I lifted wine glasses to my nose, frustrated by putting empty spoons into my mouth and then heaping ones in the next bite. This is not exactly a pleasant dining memory. The environment, however, is definitely comfortable and peaceful, and the staff are extremely kind and professional. Would normally give this 3 stars, but the food was delicious, even though I couldn't tell what half of it was (had the Western menu), and the price a good value. One small (very small thing), I did notice (and later learned that this was deliberate) there was in fact two very small lights in the otherwise pitch black dining room: a red one for a camera and a white one for the AC power. I learned that this was deliberate to give guests something to focus on, but I really wish they would cover them so there is absolutely not a speck of light in the room. Anyway, would I recommend it? Maybe. Would I go back, or go to another Noir-themed restaurant? No.

Written November 9, 2019
Germ D
Dear Jeffrey,
Thank you for visiting our restaurant and for leaving a review. I am glad you appreciate the concept.
We really try not to be perceived as a novelty or gimmicky restaurant. It is why we place a large emphasis on serving great food with great service, to which I leave you the judge of that. In essence we are still a restaurant. Of course there is blind service staff and there is no light in the dining room, however that should not take away from the actual restaurant experience.
It does indeed touch many aspects, for our guests a unique dining experience, focusing on ones “other” senses and not being distracted by phones, and for the blind and visually impaired it jobs creation and that all together raises the awareness. I am glad and grateful that is noticed and appreciated by our guests.
And then the red light, many have spoken about it. It is indeed an infrared camera and is there to keep an eye on the room and make sure our guests stay safe; we can take action if someone starts walking around or if someone is getting unwell. There is just an absence of light in the dining room and the red light is infrared and the light source for the camera. We already dimmed the light. There needs to be a balance between not too much bright light, so that it will not be distracting and still enough for the camera to see.
Some people find the light actually comforting, will others never even seem to notice it. 
We do hope you will visit us once more and maybe on the second visit you are more capable of enjoying it,
Kind regards,
Germ

This is a brilliant concept restaurant. When you arrive you are greeted and offered a surprise drink (alcoholic or non-alcoholic) and a choice of three menus, Eastern, Western or Vegetarian. You are then asked to put on a blindfold and complete a puzzle to get you used to using your sense of touch before you head into the restaurant. You are then escorted by a blind waiter to your table into a completely dark restaurant. Your waiter then shows you by touch where your cutlery and glass is. They bring out your food and explain the order that you should eat your dishes in by grabbing your hand and placing it on each dish (there are 11 dishes in total, 4 starters, 4 mains and 3 desserts). The idea is to try and guess what you are eating which isn’t as easy as it sounds. It is a surreal experience especially knowing that your partner is directly across from you but you can’t see them (or anything else for that matter). After your meal, you are led back out to the foyer where you are taken through the photos of what you ate and you find out how wrong your guesses where! It drove home to me that we do eat with our eyes as well as as other senses. If you are in Saigon, this is a must visit restaurant. Utterly brilliant experience.

reviews.review_text:
Remi
Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam22 contributions
1
An immersive experience you should do more often. Great food - value for money - unique experience.
Sep 2019 • Couples
We heard about it from friends and they were really positive about how challenging, enjoyable, sometimes confronting but mostly humbling it was. 

There you are in the welcoming area presented with a nice surprise drink and a board game to give you and idea of how to handle your food in the dark. The setting is beautiful and romantic. You learn a little about the staff and concept but you’re deliberately kept in the unknown. 

Then we met Thu, who would guide us through the evening and serve us our courses as well as tell us how we would go about eating it in a room that could only be described as pitch black (except for 1 tiny red light somewhere, check that out Germ :-). With her 3,5 year experience at the restaurant Thu was sharing a lifetime of knowledge on how to live in the dark through the simplest of things, good food paired with good wine. This is the humbling part, you’re in the most comfortable of positions to experience this but it opens you up to a discussion about it and increased awareness. 

Being foodies I can keep this part simple, the menu (we tried the eastern menu) was great. A great variety of tastes and textures cooked in a delicate way. We’ll go back, undoubtably. 

After dinner we were shown what we had actually eaten by Germ, one of 2 Founders of Noir. which resulted in a nice conversation about Asian herbs, stories about food and our desire to do this experience more often. 

In conclusion; go try it, it’s great value for money. You’ll like it and you’ll go back or you won’t like it. 

But there won’t be any part of you that thinks this isn’t an amazing experience.

reviews.review_text:
Noodles7749
Hampstead, New Hampshire63 contributions
1
Must Eat Place in Saigon
Nov 2018
For anyone that considers themselves a foodie, this is a must eat. 

You are given a welcome drink upon arrival. They give you all the "rules" of the dining room. No phones are allowed and they are locked in locker and you have the key. What I love about this place is that the servers are all blind, or nearly blind. 

When it's time to eat, the server leads you into the dining room. Each person has their hands on the shoulders of the person in front of them. They help you get settled and explain where things are on the table. It is completely dark and devoid of any light. 

They also suggest that you sit across from someone sharing the same type of meal. For example, I was seated across from my friend who also was eating the vegetarian dinner. They bring the food out and the server has you feel the plate. There were four things per plate which were in their own dishes and then slotted on a plate and they would explain which order to eat them in. There were three courses overall; appetizer, dinner, dessert. 

What an amazing experience. I'm typically pretty picky and it was terrifying and also liberating to have to completely let go and put something in my mouth that I had no idea what it was. There were only a couple of things I didn't care for, seaweed in particular. I hate seafood and that was SUPER fishy. Everything else was delicious.

When you're finished with dinner, the server leads you out and then they review what you ate. It's really interesting to see the comparison of what you thought you ate versus what you actually ate.

I highly recommend this, what an adventure!

We all were blown away at the end when the owner went through in detail what was in each dish. It was quite fascinating. The owner said they take great pride in ensuring that all the dishes are catered to allow for food intolerances because people have to place their trust in the restaurant as they can not see what they are eating and need to rely on taste and touch. This is the first place in Vietnam we encountered that had gluten free soy sauce. I also love the humanitarian component in that it has given blind and deaf people the opportunity to be able to work. I had no idea what to expect when booking for our evening at Noir other than reviews I had read but still was surprised at how I felt after our evening.

Initially you will likely be dropped at the end of a little side street which could be disconcerting but is absolutely fine like everywhere else we visited in Ho Chi Minh. There are two signs one for Blanc and one for Noir as they are part of the same restaurant family, Noir is downstairs and upon arrival you will be taken through what your experience will entail.

At the end of the experience (which feels a short time but is actually much longer than you think) you are then shown the dishes you have eaten and trust me when I say we barely guessed 2 or 3 correctly over the 11 individual dishes we were served. I will not pretend the food was Michelin star quality but thats not what you are visiting for and yes it is a little more expensive than local restaurants but still only around £30 per person equivalent currency.

Unique dining experience
Mar 2019 • Couples
So glad a friend told me about this place! It was better than I expected, and I had no idea what exactly that would be.

When you check in you get a welcome drink and an explanation about what the evening will entail, pick a cuisine and play a game blind folded to get a sense of what’s in store.

Then you are led into pitch black room with other diners and seated at your table by a blind waiter. The premise of the establishment is to employ hearing and sight impaired people while simultaneously shedding some light on what living in their world is like, for one single meal. The setup is such that your eyes never adjust; at the end of the meal I still couldn’t see my own hand right in front of me. My wife’s voice had a disembodied character floating across the table to me.

We selected the Meal from the East, which included two soups, two appetizers, four mains and three desserts. This was paired with two wines. You have no idea what you are being served, and have to use your senses of touch, taste and smell to decipher what you are consuming. We agreed on most things, but not everything, and when we were debriefed at the conclusion of our meal, we were off fifty percent of the time! All in all a wonderful, mind expanding experience. By the way, all the dishes and the wine were excellent. A true gourmet experience, albeit $40 pp.

It declined two or three times and eventually the other person paid the bill. Thought it was odd but it is a foreign card. I got home and checked the balance and I had been charged for the dinner. So we had been double charged. I immediately called the restaurant. 

The service we received from here was great - they apologised for what had happened and speaking to the manager Tam provided great reassurance that I would get the money back. I was worried as I was leaving the country shortly after this dinner. The next day the owner of Noir called to apologise and say that this would be sorted. The next day the money was back in my account - quicker than they had said it would be. 

I want to thank the owner and management for the great experience and service, both during and following the dinner. I would recommend Noir to anyone coming to HCMC.

Fantastic!
Nov 2018 • Couples
Dining in the Dark! We found this as a recommendation on Trip Advisor on our last day in HCMC. Upon entry our skills without sight were tested by a child's puzzle and a blindfold; I failed! This introduction to our evening highlighted a lot of what we take for granted and what a person with disability must compensate for.
Our blind hostess led us by hand through a series of black curtained stairs, hallways and rooms where there was nothing more than the emergency exit red LED to be seen.
We were served 11 courses of undisclosed foods, all with specific smells, textures and tastes. The trick was to identify what you were having and it is clear how much we rely on sight for some of the identification. 
The food was excellent and in good portion and they catered for my food allergy by swapping some dishes out. My wife and I didn't agree on what those dishes were!!
At the end you are shown what you've had, which leads to the discussion of how the menu items are created and the sensations you've just had. The menu is changed every 3 months so I can't, and won't, ruin the experience.
Be aware that you need to ensure your napkin is in place and that you need to stay over the bowls when you miss your mouth!! There were many stained shirts as we left.
We met and talked to an owner as we left and he explained the motivation to create the experience, especially as a foreigner living in Vietnam, and it is inspirational.

Book NOW. A-mazing!
Aug 2018 • Friends
Tucked away in a rare, sleepy-lane in downtown Saigon is this MUST visit, AMAZING concept restaurant. The Dutch owner & his partner make a strong case for the benefits of employing visual & hearing impaired beautiful souls. Many/most of the floor staff are just that and as such the degree of authenticity at Noir, 'Dining in the Dark' is very much on point. We had the pleasure of having Tsu (sorry if the spelling is wrong) look after us and it was such a beautiful, moving, INSPIRING dining experience. Tsu left the northern Vietnam region a few years ago in search of employment and a better life and suffice to say, she struck gold as did the owners of Noir. Throughout the world, it is exceptionally difficult to obtain & retain gainful employment if you are blind and this is 100% the case in Vietnam. Go to Noir, support these superb owner's and their unbelievably talented team of blind hospitality professionals. The moment you walk in to the front entrance, you feel special as you bask in the beautifully decorated lounge/bar area. After a quick rundown of how things work, an amazing welcome drink, a blind-folded 'prep' game and a confirmation of menu preferences - you are lead by hand up to the PITCH BLACK dining area. This is when the magic begins. Wave after wave of thoughtful dishes are put in front of you to devour and in our case, also paired perfectly with complementary wines brought with each course. We laughed at the end of our dinner that i had kept my glasses on the whole time as you literally cannot see 1 single thing for the entire dinner and that is the beauty of it. Take away sight and the other senses try to step up & assist in identifying menu items, wine varietals and exactly where you last put your fork down (!)

After dinner, we sat again in the lounge and the management/owner recapped the entire dinner on an ipad for us to now 'see' just what we had consumed. For example, I didn't even know Black Chicken was a thing, nor did i know that there were red dessert wines. It was all really interesting and a taste sensation from welcome drink to dessert.

This is a well run operation that is a must do for food lovers, wannabe Sommeliers and people looking for a healthy dose of inspiration when in Saigon. 6 Stars out of 5.

The ultimate experience

This quaint 2 storey restaurant boasts an eatery worthy of a five star. The twist is the restaurant offers two eating experiences. One is the standard sit down in warm lighting served by wonderful staff. The other is to experience dinner in the dark, not just dark but totally pitch black. You are greeted by your wait staff who are deaf and dumb, then you are run through the menus with staff that do talk and explain the night process. You are then led into a completely darkened room by blind staff, yes blind staff. You are delivered your selected meal of choice but not knowing exactly what’s it is. 

You then work your way around the dishes, fumbling with your cutlery until you get the hang of things. 

The whole experience is a real life test on your senses. To feel hopelessly blind, engaging your other senses to the max adjusting to lack of light.

Nearly all the staff are either totally blind and or deaf and dumb, the owner has given work, sense of purpose and confidence to people who would normally be outcasts.
The menus are very exclusive and deliver a fine dining experience. 

And at the end of the night you are given a visual of your meal just to see how well you guessed the different courses. Sadly we got about 20% right.

It is a must if you are in this part of the world.

After selecting the "menu from the west" and a wine pairing, we were presented with a quick game in which you are blindfolded and have to try to fit block-shapes into their correctly-shaped hole on a wooden board. The game is fun and gives a good introduction into how important our sense of sight is to completing even the easiest of tasks. Shortly after, we were guided to the dining room by a member of the visually-impaired staff. I can't begin to imagine how much training an discipline it takes for these staff members to be so good at their jobs. I could barely stop myself from running to walls, spilling drinks and food, but the staff always remained calm, professional, and humorous. They are extremely helpful throughout the actual dining experience, including: helping you find your glass/cup, utensils, guiding your hands to the different dishes, etc. Each dish was outstanding and we didn't even know specifically what we were eating. After the meal it was very interesting to be shown each dish that we were eating because we tried to guess each one throughout the meal. I would strongly recommend to Noir to any food lovers in HCM, couples, and groups. This place must be one of the highest quality dining experiences in the city.

Absolutely Unforgettable - no spoilers
May 2018
We visited on our 1st night to HI Chi Minh (31st May) which was also my boyfriend’s birthday. 

On arrival we were greeted with warm smiles and friendly faces and immediately taken to a casual sitting area that was well lit.
This was only the beginning of an incredibly sensual dining experience that was also life changing. 
A pleasant surprise was that we were allowed to get in touch with our senses by first being led to play a game blindfolded (sheer fun)… I won’t give away too much to ruin the fun!
Before being led by a legally blind waiter (who was friendly, spoke English, witty and accommodating) to devour a prix fixe menu (at the time of our visit we had a choice of three menus), a seeing member of staff went over all our dietary constraints and requests as we had quite a few. The customer service was exceptional from start to finish as we booked online and mentioned these similar dietary restrictions but they took the time to go over in detail to ensure our needs were met.

Points to note
• Use the restroom before being led to the dining area
• No phones or reflective clothing or accessories are allowed
• A locker is provided free of cost for all valuables (phones etc) that is monitored by a camera
• Credit cards and USD (we paid with USD cash) 
• Be prepared to have your palate stimulated and your other senses awakened 
 Did I mention they “sung” happy birthday to my boyfriend in sign language after the dining experience as we were led back to the lit area.

Professional and eloquent experience. 10 *
Jun 2018 • Couples
I came to Ho Chi Minh from China to visit my boyfriend and our last night we decided to go to this restaurant. We reserved two hours in advance and as soon as we entered we were greeted amazingly. 

We were told to sit at their lounge and were introduced to play a game. This game was to prepare us heighten our senses before entering 'la chambre noire'. As soon as we were guided inside - everything was black. The menus were to be discovered and guessed. We had an entrée, plat and dessert- the western menu. 

Whilst sitting inside my boyfriend and I could devour and take pleasure in eating the mysterious food served. It was a great experience. 

As soon as we finished, the owner himself came to sit with us and showed us the delicious food we ate. He also took the time to answer my questions about how he got the idea to install such a unique place in Vietnam. In fact, the owners hire special servers- deaf and visually impaired people to work in the restaurant. This not only made me think amazingly of the restaurant but made me feel great respect towards the owners. 

The decoration is of 'Indochine style'. As a daughter of a french art critic, I was very impressed of the way they decided to decorate the place. They wanted the restaurant to look as local as possible, and made us feel the exoticism of Vietnamese art. The owners do not segregate the local culture like most western restaurant owners, but incorporates it in their food and decoration meticulously. The food, the service, the decoration were perfect. 

Best restaurant I have been to and surpasses all the restaurants I've been to from Australia, Indonesia to France. 

Nothing but appreciation and definitely the highlight of my trip. 

Highly recommended for those wanting to indulge in an eloquent experience in Vietnam.

Absolutely mind blowing!!!
Apr 2018 • Couples
Taking the whole experiential part out of it, the quality of the food was excellent. I won't say much about it as its a surprise menu and I am not sure how often it changes but each course was great. We also had the matched wines which were all very good.
In terms of the experience I was a little bit nervous about booking it but it's been something I have wanted to try for a while. I am certainly glad that I did. The whole thing completely blew my mind. It was such a different experience not being able to see what you are eating or knowing what it is. Completely alters the whole dining experience. I guessed a few of the dishes but completely missed what others were and got quite a surprise when they told us at the end what everything was. Also had completely no idea what the wines were, which was pretty much expected anyway, I was just glad I knew what colour they were! 
The staff were excellent. I have struggled with how to write this bit as I want to acknowledge the challenges of living with a visual or hearing impairment but I don't want to condescend or make that the basis of my review. Taking all of that into account all I can say is the staff were incredibly skilled. Mind Blown

This was hands-down one of the most memorable meals of my life. Not because of the food, but the profound thoughts that this experience conjours up. First off, you dine in complete darkness. Second, is the fact that the waitstaff is comprised mostly of deaf/mute and blind people, who seamlessly execute this deeply moving experience. Now, you can take away whatever interpretation you chose. Maybe it's just you had a meal in the dark and that's it. I found myself pondering all of the nuances that sighted people take for granted, as well as the auditory experience that often goes unnoticed. I could pontificate for hours on the complete takeaway, but to keep it brief, you prepare for your journey into darkness by being blindfolded and challenged with a small game of putting uniquely'shaped wooden blocks into their respective places on a nesting board. This is meant to prepare you for your dining experience. Next, you're led to your seat by your blind server, by placing both hands on his shoulders. Once seated, and your eyes acclimate, the starter course is served, followed by the main and finally, the dessert. You are challenged after each offering to identify each of the 4 items on the plate. (only 3 in the dessert couse). This is more challenging that it sounds. I was so engulfed by the experience and deep thought that I only guessed correctly about 25% of the time. The actual food wasn't that memorable, but the experience is something I'll never forget...

Would go again, without a doubt!
Mar 2018 • Solo
Like MANY of us, Eating in the Dark is far from appealing - whats more it's a Fine Dining restaurant. Well, when you think Fine Dining, you'd automatically think of small portions, big in tastes and flavor, and impressive food presentation.

Well, Noir has it all, if not more. Denying you of your sense of sight, your other senses gets a boost - e.g. Smell and Taste. 

If you are worried about whether you will accidentally shove food up your nostrils or having your Fine Dining meal land on your lap or potentially bathing with red wine - DON'T! As long as you approach your food with extra care, smelling them first, slowly move your fork/spoon (i suggest the latter) into your food, you will almost never going to get anything on your laps (or the floor). 

My waiter (Ngaih), who is blind, made sure that it was a pleasantly unforgettable experience. He went from leading me to my table with his shoulders, to explaining where the utensils, and glasses and napkins were, to explaining what he was serving and which one to start first. 

Play a game with yourself or your partner - try to guess what each plate was - and then compare it with the answer at the end of the dinner, where you will be shown what you had. 

So glad i overcame my own skepticism and decided to go for it. It was truly an amazing experience not to be missed...

Oh, did I also mention that the food tastes excellent, too? :)

Best Dining Experience ever!
Feb 2018 • Couples
Most unusual dining experience EVER!
So we just finished a massage at a spa (best in Saigon) that our hotel referred us to that is in an ally way. We asked our spa host for the best French restaurant in the city and she referred us to the next door french restaurant that is actually two very different restaurants into one. One called Blanc (rated 5.0 stars) and one called Noir (rated 4.6 stars) and both have the best ratings. 

Blanc is the usual fine french dining....

Noir dining is in complete darkness, whereby you dine using only your smell, taste, hearing and touch. 

So you are first prepped by being blind folded then placing various shaped blocks into their space. You are given a choice of alcohol or non alcoholic drinks. This endeavor was Much harder than expected but after much giggling and the task is completed, you are then briefed on what to expect before being greeted by a blind waiter and lead upstairs by placing your hands on his shoulders to the dining area and table. I must admit, for a few seconds I thought to myself what if this is just a big hoax and we will be robbed and worse.. but the gentle waiter with his reassuring gentle mannerisms quickly removed any apprehensive thoughts. 

Using only 4 of your senses, enhances your sense of smell, taste, touch and hearing creating an atmosphere of mystery, anticipation and privacy with your dining partner that is incredible!

The food was tantalizingly delicious!!

Afterwards, we were tested to see if we can guess what each of the 11 course meals, 3 deserts and 3 wine pairings were. Although the people who ate had extensive culinary dining experiences none of us guessed more than 10 percent correct. We were blown away by the creativity and exotic mix of ingredients. This post dining briefing lasted 20 minutes. 

They have 20 waiters/servers, 11 blind and 9 deaf and mute and only speak Vietnamese sign. It takes 3 months to train the blind and one year for deaf employees before they start serving customers. 

This concept originated in Switzerland but Noir is the only restaurant in the world that serves in the dark by the blind and Deaf. 

Truly once in a lifetime must experience!

Downsides? First as you can't see what you re eating it takes away a bit of the whole experience. The portions are in fact relatively small especially if you are used to abundant rice and carbohydrates in the Vietnamese style of cooking. Nevertheless, it would be worth it to have guests offered additional portions if so desired.

The general experience , service, food, social concept of employing people with visual and hearing disabilities make it worthwhile. Moreover, price is a matter of supply and demand. Incredible experience! Delicious food
Nov 2017 • Couples
Me and my partner went here for our anniversary whilst travelling and really enjoyed ourselves! Upon arrival we were offered towel because it was pouring with rain outside so we relieved that we didn’t have to have dinner soaking wet! We were greeted and asked to sit down in the lobby area at a table while our welcome drinks were brought to us. The host talked us through the menu and what happens while you’re there, he was really lovely and spoke great English. We were given our welcome drinks after ordering and were given these puzzles to figure out whilst blindfolded, which turned out to be much more difficult than we thought! We were then asked to leave our phones and wallet in a locker prior to dining to stop distractions. I would also advise using the bathroom before dinner as it will ruin your dinner having to get up and walk out. We were taken to our waitress for the evening who was blind and absolutely lovely, before holding on to each other’s shoulders conga line style up into the dark dining room. The meals were amazing, it was so cool having to guess what you were eating the whole time and describing it to your partner. Afterwards we were shown out and back into the lobby for another drink while the host goes through everything that you ate. It’s amazing how little you know what you’re eating until you’re told what it is. At the end, we were given ponchos soon leaving which was a nice touch as the rain hadn’t stopped. Overall the experience was really worth it, we were really happy we chose to eat here.

There, we put on blindfolds and tried putting blocks into the correct holes. I crushed it - because I sleepwalk a lot! At that time, we chose what menu we preferred - Vietnamese, Western or Vegetarian. But that's all we were told, and we picked Vietnamese. We could hear our server's voice, and that of a Spanish group some feet away. Our server instructed us how we were going to each - no chopsticks, a fork and a spoon. Four bowls came out on one plate for an appetizer, and we were told to eat clockwise. Same for the main course. The dessert was three straight items on one plate. There was only one thing I didn't particularly like during the app phase. The rest of the dinner was magnificent. We were led back to the foyer, where were showed on an iPad what we ate. reviews.review_text:
AdamMoore1
Prague, Czech Republic105 contributions

Must go - for many reasons
Oct 2017 • Couples
We had pre-booked Noir and glad we did. It is a restaurant where you get to eat in the dark, waiters & some other staff are blind or visually impaired and the whole restuarant supports the Vietnamese association for blind. You arrive and pick from menu the type (Eastern/Western) menu, then they give you a blindfold and you play a couple of sensory games before being led by your blind guide to your table. The room is completely black and you really can't see anything around you, but you are told where your cutlery and glasses are. You can orientate fairly easily once you know this. Then the food comes out and each course has four tasting options. The food is excellent and really good fun trying to guess what you are eating when you can't see - especially difficult with the unfamiliar ingredients. All our dishes were great - we had the wine pairing and the wine was not so good (this is a rule in Vietnam), but again added to the fun on what you are drinking - we made one really big guessing error there which surprised me. However, the benefit of the wine pairing being in glasses became apparent when we hear a crash, and a guy at another table saying sorry I split the bottle, and it was all over them and the bottle was red! After the meal you get shown pictures of what you ate and explained the ingredients in them. Really good - and we got most of the main content right, although I admit that I mistook beef for duck (I blame the plum sauce it came with confusing me) . The whole concept is brilliant and different and the fact it supports the local blind community who do not get many other opportunities is a huge plus.

Looking for a place to have dinner with colleagues, we were intrigued by the concept of eating in the dark, and conforted by the great reviews. A group of 8 people, we were greeted by the friendly staff and started the little introduction blind game. Then we proceeded to the dark room. First thing: it was FREEZING cold. When we mentioned it, we got...blankets... and were still cold. We proceeded with dinner anyway. Service is good, the food was enjoyable. Here, the dishes are all in bowls and pre-cut in mouthfuls, for easy consumption. At the end, you go back to the light and they show and tell you what you had. Basically, If you always wanted to do that, go and cross it off your list. Food is good and service is OK. But for me it was an overpriced gimmick, good not great food, and we froze to death.

Written October 20, 2017
Germ D
Dear Frenchy-in-Bavaria,
Thank you for choosing Noir. Dining in the Dark and I am pleased you feel the service was good and the food enjoyable.
I am sorry that you feel the room was cold. We do indeed have scarves on hand in cases like this. We have readjusted the A/C settings already.
I am saddened to hear that you feel the experience is a gimmick; we are trying everything we can not to avoid that. As you have no doubt read, the vast majority of our guests thoroughly enjoy their dining experiences and do not call it a gimmick at all. I regret you feel that way.
In essence we are still a restaurant; we try our effort to serve great food with great service, to which I leave you the judge of that. Of course there is blind service staff and there is no light in the dining room, however that should not take away from the actual restaurant experience.
We still do pay attention to presentation too, there is a high level of integrity in our team.
Dining in the dark does touch many aspects, for you as a guest is a unique dining experience, focusing on ones “other” senses and not being distracted by phones, secondly it provides us to create jobs for the blind and visually impaired and thirdly that all together raises the awareness into the blind community and one gets to understand better how our senses work.
Of course it is not easy to identify the dishes in the dark, that is true.
However you are definitely focusing more on taste, smell and textures. Not that you get all of a sudden superhuman tasting skills and can identify everything, nobody has told you that. 
Since 70% of our sense is sight, our other senses are not that strong anyway. Though, in the dark with 30% left for four senses there is indeed an overload on your senses; taste and smell heighten, you will start to touch everything around you and the texture of the food is suddenly more noticeable, also one’s hearing does become intensified.
We take sight quite for granted and you definitely came to the conclusion, or at least confirmed the fact, that we are eating with our eyes.
Imagine how many meals you have in your life, out of those thousands of meals in the light once in your life having a meal that you cannot see is not that bad, would it be?
Thank you for your review and we do hope you will reconsider to visit us another time,
Kind regards,
Germ

Made our trip to HCMC extra memorable
Sep 2017 • Friends
So there are a couple of dining in the dark restaurants around the world, but Noir. Dining in the Dark was my first time visiting a restaurant of the sort. As per all restaurants in HCMC the interior decor is faultless. There are modern art pieces and decorations with traditional Vietnamese interior design, the entrance and the lounge was spacious, airy and comfortable.

We were first greeted with welcome cocktails and had to complete a kiddie puzzle game blindfolded for us to get used to our senses. Then the owner came to us to explain how the mystery menu and the mystery wine pairing worked. We were then introduced to our waitress, who is blind and went through 3-4 months training before joining the restaurant, who led us into the pitch black dining area. Even though my heart started to feel heavy as I wondered in my mind how uncomfortable I felt in the dark but this is everyday life to her, the team really made the whole experience fun as they chat to us and joked about our clumsiness.

We went for the "East" menu, and the food was exceptional! Made special because I'm a picky eater, and there was no way for me to pick out those loathed cucumbers in the dark, so I ended up experiencing the burst of flavours instead of just eating what I thought I should like to eat.

The hostess then showed us what our food should look like after we re-entered the lounge area.

The whole 3-course meal with wine pairing came to a total of GBP35-40/person. 

For the environment, atmosphere, service and quality of food, I give this place 10 out of 10!!!!

Amazing Solo Experience
May 2017 • Solo
Saigon was the last stop on a month long trip from North to South in Vietnam and though on a backpacker's budget, I decided to splurge on this experience. It was well worth it!

First the splurge cost no more than what I would have spent on an average night out in a restaurant at home in New York City. But, even if it had, this experience still would have been great.

I was travelling alone and couldn't get any of my companions to join me, so after a bit of hesitation, I decided to go alone. And I'm so glad I did. 1) No one knows you are alone - it is pitch black after all. And there are other people in the dining room who are chatting so its not like its silent. 2) I imagine that not being worried about engaging in conversation or commenting on how weird it all felt, meant that I was really focused on tasting the food and really feeling the darkness. It was really cool! 3) The food was delicious - I had the vegetarian menu so I didn't have to worry about any strange mystery meats. Still there was a great variety of flavors and textures and it was fun to try to guess what I was eating. 4) It wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be to get adjusted and somehow my waiter always knew exactly when I was done with a course and ready for the next. 5) The debrief at the end where they tell you what you've eaten and show you pictures was fun!

Overall, everyone I encountered was friendly and good at whatever they were there to do. The food was really tasty and the experience unique.

If you are thinking about doing this, but are unsure or don't have anyone to go with, go anyway! You won't regret it.

So, we've always wanted to go to a 'eat in the dark' restaurant and when I found this one I was so happy! What made it stand out was that the whole waitstaff is blind, legally blind or deaf. 
You first go in and are asked to pick what type of menu you will have. Eastern, Western or Vegetarian. It's suggested you get the same menu as your group so you can talk about it. They also reassure you that they will serve nothing crazy!
Then you are to do a little game to help with the dinner. 
You are then lead through the dark up to the dining room. The waitstaff is very good and very easy to understand. You are taken care of the whole time. 
When they say the dining room is dark, they are not exaggerating! You can see NOTHING! I found it helped to keep my eyes closed, otherwise I got tired trying to focus on something. 
The food was amazing! Was fun trying to figure out what we were eating! It was totally normal too!

reviews.review_text:

Interesting concept, not enjoyable food
Aug 2017 • Family
We came to Noir after a recommendation from a friend and upon reading all of the fantastic reviews on TripAdvisor. Please note that most reviews here refer to the experience rather than the food. Let me explain...

I dined with my mom and sister. I am vegetarian and they are not. Our host persuaded me to order the Asian menu so that we could share more of our experience together and assured me it would be amended minimally only to exclude meat. I said that eggs and fish were okay and then asked for extra reassurance that there would be no meat products used. Yes, I was told. I still approached with a lot of apprehension, but tried to relax about it.

The room is indeed pitch black and my sister promptly poked herself in the eye with her beverage straw while feeling around. We laughed too loud about this and were told to quiet down. My dining companions felt rather claustrophobic, but I was enjoying the simplicity of the darkness.

Our first course was served and I promptly bit into an octopus tentacle. Not what I was expecting and I immediately regretted not just ordering the full vegetarian meal. As this was only my second night it Vietnam, I had not yet learned to be more specific that by saying I eat fish means I only eat fish...no shellfish or other sea animals. From here on out, I did not much enjoy the eating experience and practiced touching my food before eating it, selectively only choosing what I could surely identify with my fingertips. My anxiety overrode any enjoyment of the food. I can't really say that I liked anything, but I also can't untangle whether this was due to the actual food or just not being able to see and know any of it. My mom and sister felt likewise and we were itching to leave and also in need of a restroom, but not sure of the procedure for using it. The time between courses and being excused from the dining room seemed to stretch on forever. 

Back in the safety of the light, another host sat us down to view what we ate. He said to me, "And you are the one that doesn't eat meat, but meat product is okay, so your menu was a little bit different. I grimaced a bit, but did not want to make a big deal about it because by this point we'd been there for 2.5 hours and were late to massage appointments! 

The food we were showed on the iPad looked very gorgeous, but did not so much taste that way when we ate it. There are so many flavors and ingredients with each dish that it is hard to pick much of anything out in terms of taste. I wonder what the experience would be like if the dishes were simpler and not so complex and focused instead just on the quality of a few ingredients. What is the point of such minute detail if it cannot be seen or tasted?

If you are looking for an experience over nourishment and a whole evening event then this is the place for you. It's also great that they give jobs to a population that otherwise would not have such an opportunity. I recommend you don't go here hungry and if you are the only vegetarian in your party, order the vegetarian meal or go somewhere else.
Read more
Written August 19, 2017
Germ D
Dear WanderVV,
Thank you for visiting us and for leaving a review.
I am glad you liked the service and appreciate the concept and our employment of blind and visually impaired staff. I regret that you did not enjoy the food. I am sorry to hear.
Having the same menu does indeed enhance the experience and lets one talk about the dishes together. If one has a different menu, one may feel excluded from the conversations. If you had requested for pure vegetarian, we would have served you this menu. However, since you mentioned you will have fish, but not meat, it is easy for us to take out the meat from the same menu as your sister and mother ordered, where for you the meat is taken out. That is why we suggested you to the take same. 
I do believe we have asked if besides fish seafood would be fine. Apologies if it was not clear enough.
We have many guests, quite a few vegetarians too. Non of the guests are the same and there are many variations to the dietary requests; without meat, but with fish, or vegetarian without egg, but dairy all right etc. We do ask, since you know your requests best. However, if you do not inform us, it is difficult to change. We are flexible, but we just need to know.
We are still a restaurant, of course there is no light in the dining room and the service staff is blind, however that should not take away from an actual hospitality experience. The chefs in our kitchen team take pride in making sure the dishes prepared are being fully enjoyed by our guests, we place a lot of effort in the development, preparation and even presentation of the food. If the dishes would be too simple, one may complain that it is too simple. The dishes in the menus we serve are not that different from dishes you may find on other lit restaurants.
Our sense of sight is indeed very dominant and there fore the other senses are not as strong. In the dark taste and smell heighten, you are more focused on it, however it remains a challenge to identify to different ingredients, that is normal. Though we feel we should not simplify the menus, we still like our guests to enjoy a meal.
I regret that the experience was not what you hoped for, and I am sorry we failed in exceeding your expectations. Still I hope you will consider visiting us once your travels bring you back to Saigon,
Kind regards,
Germ

In the dark obviously the taste, the smell and the texture are more at the foreground. Of course nobody is able to see it, but that does not mean that we do not take care of the presentation, it certainly does matter. Dining in the dark does heighten senses, although it is still difficult to guess the ingredients correctly.
It happens quite frequently that one claims not to eat ingredients in the light, however in the dark with just taste and smell and not knowing what the ingredients are, actually starts liking it. Sometimes people even say it was actually their most favourite dish.

It's the nicest dark experience you'll have.

We booked weeks in advance, not sure that's necessary but it was a must do (rather than a must-see cos you can't !! :)). Our booking was 6pm and though only 4km away the taxi ride took over 45mins in peak traffic so arrived 20mins late. Bookings are held only 15mins according to their site but we didn't want to test them on it given the popularity. Very friendly welcome was marred by bizarre request to move to outside table to give way for a big group arrival. We wouldn't budge and they politely rolled with it. Guided in my beautiful blind guide. Husband freaked as he's claustrophobia and though had prepped himself, the sudden plunge into complete blackness triggered anxiety. Staff and owner handled him sensitively and he joined us again minutes later, thus completing our family unit again. We had not a clue and apart from one or two food items couldn't guess. Goes to show the zilch mindful eating we do. I dipped into rather than ate starters as the feel of the foods was freaking me out. But devoured the main and dessert cos I wasn't going to waste our money ! Upside is: we sampled foods that we wouldn't ordinarily try and we talked a lot about the taste, feel and smell of offerings. Our vegan daughter had her own menu which she was delighted about. It's disorienting eating and being together in the dark. Despite the removal of devices, watches that emit light etc beforehand, a patron at the next table took a photo. there's always bloody one, isn't there. the restaurant is beautifully appointed with great artwork and ornately tasteful furniture. it's gives off a high class venue and the staff provide quality care and attention. We were given the great reveal afterwards. the toilets are the best anywhere. Gotta do. Gotta experience. It's worth the $190NZ for a family of four (with teens).

reviews.review_text:
maryyeo
Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam4531 contributions

Lovely marriage of sensory, social advocacy & food appreciation
Mar 2017 • Couples
A visit to Noir is definitely not just for the food (which is fabulous, too), but for the entire experience --- one of sensory adventure and standing up for a social cause.

We loved everything about this meal down to the details:
- corner location of a quiet alley adds to its secretive charm
- beautiful lobby interior with an Old Shanghai-nese theme oozing from the corner spiral stairs to the exquisite wooden furniture that it kinda transports you (or your mind) to a time long, long ago... and although the wait for our turn was rather long (45min on a weekday night), the beautiful lobby & friendly staff definitely helps in making us more patient
- while waiting, we got to enjoy the juice/cocktail served and also play some sensory games blindfolded to prepare us for our dining in pitch black darkness later on. The staff was always observant and quick to replace a new game for us once we were done with one.
- the sensory experience in the dark is what everyone's here been talking about - heightened listening and taste buds - we actually quite enjoyed the "intrusion" from other diners since the husband and I were happily guessing what accent/nationality each diner was from. And of course we enjoyed the absolute focus on each other with no phone distractions whatsoever.
- food was beyond our expectations because the owner and/or chef was able to introduce so many detailed elements into each dish and we had so much fun guessing what each ingredient and seasonings were. The final "reveal" at the end by individual service staff, and the owner himself (!) was such a treat because it brings a full circle to this experience, not only being finally able to see the beautiful pictures of the food we ate, but also appreciating the thoughtfulness of every single taste nuances added by every single ingredient.
- best of social advocacy - this was our FAVOURITE reason of dining here... it was amazing when the owner revealed to us at the end that the blind waiters/waitresses who spoke superb English were graduates in political sciences, law degrees, etc. - that just makes us appreciate their warm, gentle service a million times more and wanting to get to know them more as individual persons, not just as their "blind waiter" status

We were also quite pleased to find out that they change their menus every month or was it 3 weeks... I can't remember. So that's a good reason to return too. Price-wise, we found it very reasonable for fine dining. It would have costed us at least double at a restaurant with a similar concept (but maybe not as fun since we know the menu before eating...), NOX, in Singapore...

reviews.review_title: Review at Noir Dining In The Dark
reviews.review_text:
John T
Los Angeles, California13 contributions
1
The Western menu was a bit disappointing, but service was fantastic!
Apr 2017 • Couples
First off, let me start this review by saying we decided to go with the Western Menu. So the food portion of the review is for the Western menu. After a week of eating nothing but Vietnamese food, we decided a change of taste. If I had to go back, I would've probably opted for the Eastern menu. We were after all in Vietnam right?

Cost of the "Menu from the West" was 650,000 VND per person, approximately $30 USD. Drinks are of course extra and optional. It's not a bad price for the quality (not taste...we'll get to that below) and the overall experience. 

First your seated in the front lounge area as you await your server. The dining experience first starts off with two complimentary drinks, either alcoholic or non-alcoholic. The drinks are then followed by a game, where you are blinded folded and you attempt to place a variety of different shapes in it's proper shaped location. The game is intended for you to get used to the feeling of interacting in completely in the dark. It's actually a lot harder than it looks, but somewhat fun!

After you are done with the game, you are then escorted by a waiter (who is visually impaired) directly to the dining area which is completely pitch black. You are than seated at your table and given instructions From there, you are served a total of 3 plates, somewhat of a tasting menu. The first plate is 4 different types of appetizers, than 4 types of main courses, then 3 types of desserts. The food to me just was not very good. The food was prepared properly, but the flavors itself seemed to overcomplicate itself with the intention of wanting to throw you off and have you second guess what you ate. I guess that's the whole point, but it just didn't want me over. I wasn't expecting to be blown away, but I the same time I definitely was not satisfied. Again, I want to reiterate that I went with the Western menu. Maybe the Eastern menu may have been better. 

After you're done with the menu, you than seat you down and give you a very personal overview of what you just ate. You also have the option of ordering additional drinks. 

noir. is a "true" dining in the dark expensive - It's just you, your food, and your waiter. The rest is up to your imagination. I've been to other dining in the dark experiences before, so I've may have been spoiled. The others I've been too had bit more interaction between the waiter and the diners that made the experience somewhat fun, and I just didn't get that here. Again, I could be comparing apples to oranges, so take that with a grain of salt. 

Probably would not go here again, but I do want to commend noir. for hiring workers that might have a tougher time finding work in this type industry.

A MUST DO!!
Apr 2017 • Couples
After stumbling across this restaurant on trip advisor, researching and gathering the concept that Noir has to offer, I hesitantly booked a table for my fussy eating partner and I. 

We arrived, both nervous. The staff were lovely. Firstly greeting us, talking us through the process, what to expect as well as what to do if any issues were to arise. 

We were then given a mystery cocktail, and a menu to select from. We selected our menu and explained our dietary requirements, the staff were really understanding about these and were able to cater to them.

After a game to introduce ourselves to the darkness we were taken to the dining area to meet our guide Bao and begin the experience. 

Bao lead us to our table describing what was in front of us, before bringing out our first dish. We then continued on to our main and the dessert. 

Afterwards we were taken back into the entrance were we collected our belongings, settled the bill and were taken through each and every dish we had tried. 

I must admit, I didn't enjoy everything on offer throughout the 3 courses, some due to taste, others texture, but eating the unknown, in the pitch black dark allowed myself and partner to taste and enjoy things we wouldn't usually attempt. 

We commend the overall hospitality of the staff, and effort that has gone into creating not only this restaurant but entire experience.

Written April 17, 2017
Germ D
Dear Dmitry,
Thank you for your message, and I am very sorry to hear that you do not like the concept of our restaurant.
It must be quite frustrating, indeed, to take the time to go to a restaurant with expectations only to notice those can not be met.
We are a dining in the dark restaurant, a restaurant still, but indeed without light in the dining room and with service staff who are blind and visually impaired. But what is wrong with the concept? We are proud of it.
We provide a unique dining experiences, focusing on ones “other” senses of taste and smell. 70% of our sense is sight and in the dark with 30% left for four senses there will be an overload on your senses; taste and smell heighten, you will start to touch everything around you and the texture of the food is suddenly more noticeable, also one’s hearing does become intensified. We take sight quite for granted and you would definitely have come to the conclusion, or at least confirmed the fact, that we are eating with our eyes. 
Secondly it provides us to create jobs for the blind and visually impaired and that all together raises the awareness. In countries like Vietnam about 94% of the blind population is unemployed.
I understand that there are indeed people to who do not like the concept. And that is fine, I respect that. Sight is a big part of our meals. 
However, to write a bad review just based on the dislike of the concept, before even trying it, is quite something.
Where did we fail? What did we do to deserve your one bubble rating?
You say there is no choice, of course you have a choice, sir, you do have. You have chosen to visit our restaurant, however if you do not like the concept or cuisine, you have the choice of not coming.
If for instance I do not like mushroom, I make the choice of not going to a mushroom hotpot restaurant, but I shall not write a bad review because of my dislike of mushrooms.
If I choose a restaurant just based on the rating and do not look further to understand the restaurant, well, who’s mistake is it then? The restaurant failing to inform the guest, or the guest failing to look into further information?
Do we fail to inform our guests with the concept? There is a lot of information on the TripAdvisor website, see the name of our restaurant, the pictures, the reviews of other guests, the description of the concept, further there is our own website and social media describing the concept of the restaurant quite precisely. 
I believe, we do not fail or hide to inform our guest what the concept is. 
Is it too much to ask to reconsider your review? In my humble opinion, all together, it is quite unfair to give the restaurant a one bubble rating just based on the dislike of the concept, especially since you did not experience it.
Kind regards,
Germ

Dark and delicious
Mar 2017 • Family
The experience of Noir is worth the price of the ticket. The food was delicious for the most part. There were a few pieces that I would not have ordered on my own but that is part of the experience. A word to the wise, leave the kids at home. The darkness can be a bit overwhelming.
Value
Service
Food
Review collected in partnership with this restaurant 
Written April 11, 2017
Germ D
Dear Doha Wolf,
Thank you for your review and it was a pleasure welcoming you to our restaurant.
I am glad you liked the dinner and experience of eating in the dark.
Dark it is indeed, and that does heighten the other senses, not that you all of a sudden have super-human tasting skills, however your attention is much more focused on taste, texture and smell.
And of course you might have eaten ingredients in the dark you may not automatically have ordered in the light. You definitely came to the conclusion, or at least confirmed, the fact that we are eating with our eyes.
For sure we do take our senses for granted, but here at Noir. Dining in the Dark we learn how to appreciate them. As the menus are not disclosed beforehand and no one is able to see during dinner, we want to ensure our diner feel comfortable and confident as they enjoy their dinner. So, our guides are trained to explain the table setting, how each course is laid out and where to begin. 
For children, though, it can be a very interesting experience as well, educational even. First you get to understand more how our senses are working (or not working, in the dark) and secondly it creates awareness into the blind community as well; how, regardless their lack of sight, a blind person is more than capable of working. Of course for some children it may be too much.
Thank you for the recommending words and we do look forward to welcoming you back,
Kind regards,
Germ
