reviews.review_title: Review at Noir Dining In The Dark
reviews.review_text:
Tomy P
Hanoi, Vietnam125 contributions
1
Amazing set menu and unforgettable experience
Mar 2017 • Friends
We had no chance to enjoy food here at the first day because we did not make the reservation in advance. On the next day, we had to make a call to reserve before coming there.
We had two options to choose to enjoy lunch. Enjoying as normal and in a dark room. We of course chose the second. Before entering to the room and enjoying lunch, we had to practise a example that mean they gave us a puzzle game with many sharps and the mission was how to put them exactly in the the indicated hole in a small board.
After completing the practice, we were introduced by Duong who is blinded and he would lead us to the room and enjoy lunch.
Oh my god, the sky seemed collapsed when entering to the dark room. We had to touch and hear what was going on and indicate where the spoon, the chopsticks were.
There were some Western, Korean, Chinese guests having luch too. Truthfully It was not easy to guess what we ate and I felt stressed sometimes.
Finally, we finished and got out the room by Duong. We came to the lobby and another staff showed us what we ate. 
Funny but stressed when enjoying lunch like that. And it is not suitable for business man.
Read more
Written March 27, 2017
Germ D
Dear Tomy,
Thank you for visiting our restaurant for lunch and for writing a review.
I am pleased you liked the food and the service of Duong.
Besides having a unique dining experience in the dark and job creation for the blind and visually impaired, this concept also allows our guests to get a better insight into the life and work of the blind.
It can be rather unnatural at first, there is suddenly absolutely no light in the dining room and in our lives there is always light around us. We are very depended on sight, and that is something we take very much for granted. We want to ensure our diners feel comfortable and confident as they enjoy their dinner. So, our guides are trained to explain the table setting, how each course is laid out and where to begin. 
We feel we offer a unique dining opportunity and everyone is welcome, as long as one is coming open minded. And, indeed, it is definitely recommended to make reservations prior, in order to avoid disappointment, since on many evenings we are being booked up fast.
I am afraid you are mistaken, chopsticks we do not have and we only offer one dining opportunity, that is dining in the dark. We are about to open a second restaurant in the light indeed, however to is yet to open.
It would be nice to welcome you back again, once you revisit Saigon,
Kind regards,
Germ

recipeforlife
London, United Kingdom89 contributions

Unique and humbling
Mar 2017 • Friends
As a one off experience this is certainly worth considering. At the start you are given a little blindfolded game to play, by one of the deaf and dumb staff, to get you familiarised before being led into a black room by your blind waitress. It's best if you all choose the same menu so you can try to work out what each dish is. We went Western as I didn't fancy any more spicy food and thought it might be easier to work out what the ingredients were. At the end they show you what you had although the photos are of the ingredients beautifully arranged and not how they would appear in the serving dish, I think they should show you what it really looked like. We got elements of most dishes correct and one horribly wrong! 
I wasn't overly impressed with the food though. Wasn't bad, just not special.
Now whether that was due to not being able to see it I will never know. All the staff were amazing. So, a unique experience, recommended to try once.
Read more
Review collected in partnership with this restaurant 
Written March 27, 2017
Germ D
Dear Noir.-guests,
Thank you for choosing Noir. Dining in the Dark and for sharing your impressions.
We enjoyed having you over for dinner and I am glad you liked the dinner in the dark and found the service team amazing.
Dark it is, and that does heighten the other senses, not that you all of a sudden have super-human tasting skills, however your attention is much more focused on taste, texture and smell.
It is on itself of course a good idea to show the pictures of the dishes how they were served, although since the ingredients are mixed and cut in smaller pieces, it is more difficult to see what the ingredients actually are. That is why we focus more on the ingredients in the dishes on the pictures we show at the end of the dinner.
It is not a guarantee to guess better taking the menu with food you are more familiar with, if you would have taken the other menu it would have been equally difficult to guess ingredients; most of our guests say they can guess 50-60% of the ingredients regardless if they have selected the Menu from the East or the Menu from the West.
Thank you for the recommending words and we do look forward to welcoming you back again,
Kind regards,
Germ

reviews.review_text:

Amazing dining experience!
Feb 2017 • Couples
Of all the restaurants we booked for our trip to Vietnam, I was most looking forward to dining at Noir! The entire experience of dining in the dark sounded thrilling and it definitely lived up to, and exceeded my expectations. I don't want to give too much away, but essentially we arrived just before our 7pm reservations and in the waiting area we were given a mystery welcome cocktail and had the chance to play some games that attempt to prepare you to use senses other than sight. We then reviewed the food and drink menus to place our order before we were seated. For the menus, the individual dishes are a mystery so you simply pick an "East" or "West" inspired menu. My husband and I both selected the "East" menu and splurged for the wine pairing with each course. After using the restroom one last time and stowing our belongings in a locker, we were led outside and over to where we would be dining. We met our waiter for the evening whose name was Tu. Most of the employees here are blind or have another type of handicap and I think this is a wonderful way for them to put their talents to use and show other people an extraordinary time. 

We were led up a series of stairs and through turns in a sort of train with our hands on the person's shoulders in front of us. At this point, I must admit I got a bit nervous. How would we find our seat? How would we eat and drink without everything spilling on the floor? All of these fears were unfounded, however, as Tu expertly led us to our seat and explained the layout of the table. The meal consisted of three courses - the appetizers and main each had four small dishes and the dessert three. The food is served on a wooden board on which the small bowls fit. So if you are careful to pick up the bowl and your fork and get up close and personal, you'll be fine! Same with the drinks - I just made sure to move slowly and always put my glass back in the same spot and it was fine. My husband and I had a lot of fun trying to figure out what we thought each dish was and listening to the other diners around us (there were only two other tables in the room we were in while we dined). After the meal was over, Tu led us out the way we came and we sat in the sitting area while a staff member went over the entire menu (with pictures!) and wine selection. Boy were we wrong on some of the dishes! In addition, you completely lose your sense of time while dining in the dark. I felt like we were blowing through the meal and would have guessed that only 45 minutes past, but in actuality it was an hour and a half! This dining experience was one of the most unique and fun I've ever had. I would not hesitate to do it again or recommend it to anyone in Saigon. Although it was definitely one of the most expensive meals on our trip (USD 100.00), it was well worth the splurge!

What an Experience
Feb 2017 • Couples
We dined here after reading reviews as it sounded like fun and with a good dining experience.

We were not disappointed. First of all, the concept is explained to you and you're given a blindfold to wear and asked to put different shaped objects into a wooden board, working purely by touch. The idea is to try and give an impression of how the world works when you are deprived of sight, and so experience the meal by taste/texture. 

After depositing watches, gsm's in a locker you are guided by your waiter to your table by placing your hands on his shoulders. This is in complete darkness with no light whatsoever and the waiters explain where your table/seats/cutlery are and how to navigate the service.

The meals come in mini trays divided into 3/4 and you work around them in a clockwise direction. After each course, you are asked to describe what you have eaten based only on taste and texture. I was surprisingly bad when deprived of my sight!!

The staff are either blind or mute and provide fantastic service, equally the food is of the highest quality.

We're very glad to have experienced Noir, thank you.

Was unsure about this concept of eating in the dark but I am pleased to say it was a fantastic experience. The staff were excellent from start to finish. We started off with a welcome drink and a couple of games with a blindfold on to work on the hand co-ordination. We then choose which menu we would like we choose western and was told no food would have a bad taste etc there was also a eastern and veggie option. We also picked the mystery wine so you got a different wine with each course. All phones and watches were put in lockable drawers so you don't spoil the atmosphere. We met our waiter Bow who was blind and he took us into the restaurant he showed us to our table and pointed out where everything was and where he would put our food. As each course came it consisted of 4 small portions of different starters, main course and desert. Each one was fabulous and I enjoyed every single one. Me and husband talked about each dish to see if we could recognize the ingredients. Now would ask us if we knew what certain dishes were but all will be revealed at the end. reviews.review_text:

Wokingham, United Kingdom60 contributions

A truly memorable experience
Feb 2017
It isn't often that you have a dinner experience to savour, but we did at Noir.

- 3 menus on offer - Eastern, Western and Vegetarian. You are recommended to have the same as others in your party so you can talk about what you are eating with them, which we did - choosing the Eastern menu. The menus are available online, but I would recommend taking the plunge and just picking one - guessing what you are eating rather than knowing is much more fun!

- The food was great - 11 dishes in all (4 starters, 4 mains, 3 desserts), all relatively small portions but it adds up over 11 courses and we were nicely fully when we left. Not every dish was to our tastes, but that is the point of the tasting menu - to broaden horizons.

- The whole experience has been meticulously created with the customer in mind. You enter into a reception room, which leads to a bar. These rooms (and even the restroom) have bright, vivid and interesting pieces of art / sculpture to look at, heightening your sense of sight before it is taken away from you in the dining room! Whilst in the reception room you are served drinks and are given a blind fold and a block puzzle to complete with your blind fold on, preparing you for what is to come. After that you are led through to the dining room where you are introduced to your waiter, who guides you to your table, explains how the meal will work and then serves your food and drink.

- The experience of eating in the dark is superb - we found ourselves smelling the food as it arrived, talking about every dish and savouring the flavours - far more than we normally would. What a great way to enjoy a meal!

- It is great that this restaurant has created jobs for those with sight, hearing and speaking disabilities. The staff are attentive, helpful and converse very well in English.

- Please note, the dining room is completely pitch black, you will not be able to see your hand in front of your face. We heard a group in the reception room debating about whether it was really what they wanted to do as one of the party wasn't good in the dark - if you aren't give up your reservation for someone who will appreciate the experience!

We hadn't done a dining in the dark experience before, but would recommend it to anyone to try - Noir was a great example and we would eat there again.

I came to Noir with my husband and some friends visiting Ho Chi Minh City. We were greeted by a friendly staff who eased us into the experience with some sensory games. We were blindfolded and assigned a couple of tasks to get accustomed to working without our sense of sight. We were asked to choose a style of food for our dinner set, but we were not told the specifics of the menu. Two of the people in our group chose the vegetarian option and the rest chose the eastern option. I'd highly recommend choosing a set with at least one other person so you can discuss as you eat. We were led upstairs by our waiter using our sense of touch and verbally given instruction throughout the meal. Physical guidance was only offered when absolutely necessary. After our meal, one of the staff members sat with us and went over each portion of our 3-course menu explaining what we ate. While I could describe each aspect of our visit in detail, the sensation of losing access to one of our senses for an extended period of time is indescribable. Germ D
Dear Duc,
Thank you for your continuous support of our restaurant and for writing a review.
It has been always a pleasure to welcome you and your family and I am pleased you consider the food to be above average.

I have read your review with attention and there are some topic I like to shed some light at. I really regret you feel upset with the service of our restaurant.
Firstly, we always try our best to welcome our guests, however it is definitely recommended to make reservations prior, in order to avoid disappointment, since on many evenings we are being booked up fast. Luckily we were able to seat you without a reservation.
Secondly, we do encourage our diners to explore the complete "gastronomic journey" through our menu, putting aside one's likes or dislikes, one might realise that a lot of likes and dislikes are just confirmed by the eyes and not necessarily by the taste and smell. We have chosen very day-to-day ingredients - of course one might not be familiar with some of those – however there are so to say no “strange” ingredients on the menu. We would not be pleasing anyone with that.
If there are any allergies or dietary restriction in general, and those a bit more out of the ordinary in particular, we do wish to know before, so we make sure those ingredients in question do not end up in the meal. You know your allergy best, so please let us know. If you like us to take that serious, we appreciate your seriousness in this as well and tell us in advance.
Your request of no onion and garlic in a vegetarian menu is realistic, not very common, but we can do, IF we only have time to prepare the dishes. It is not feasible to prepare that on the spot, with no prior request, hence we could not cater for this request.
An allergy for no nuts for instance is easy, we just take out the nut. Of course nuts is not an ingredients we use in many dishes, there might be one or two dishes to alter.
Your request for no onion and no garlic, ingredients that are used in many dishes makes matters a bit more complicated, especially since our stocks, which are on the base of many sauces, are made with onion.
We simply cannot cater for that if we have not had the time to prepare for that.
Besides that, I doubt the link of no onion and no garlic and the state of being pregnant, for sure can can take out raw cheese, raw eggs, raw meat and fish. 
For dietary requests, based on allergies, pregnancy, belief, or religious purposes we have to and can cater for. For likes and dislikes we like our guests to give it a go.

Another comment is that we do recommend our guests to take the same menu, as it enhances the experience; it is nice to talk about and discuss the different ingredients in the menu. As I understand your requests of choosing different menus were not based on allergies, just on preferences.

Written December 23, 2016
Germ D
Dear Kevin,

Thank you very much for your visit last week and Merry Christmas! The team, my partner Tú and I hope you have had nice a Christmas time during your holiday here in Vietnam.
I have, of course, taken notice of your review on TripAdvisor which I have read with attention.
 
I am pleased you enjoyed the dinner and found the experience very nice until the moment of payment. It seems that until that point you had a great night with nothing to complain about, including the quality of the service and the food served. Thank you as I am most grateful for that. I am very sad to read the rest of your review.
 
However, I think we have to see the incident of not being able to pay by card in a fair light.
Unfortunately, and very regretfully, we were not able to let you pay by both of your credit cards, as we explained, the bank we have an account with, the VietComBank - the largest and most respectable bank in Vietnam - faced malfunction in their system. It was not maintenance, it had nothing to do with your card, or with our credit card machine (we tried both terminals, with both of your cards); it was a failure of the connectivity of the bank, because their line broke down. It was out of our control and we were depending on maintenance personnel of the bank. As matter of fact this affected other companies and other guests as well, and indeed I have called some friends at other restaurants and they had faced the same issue.
We called the bank and they mentioned it would take 10 minutes to fix, however indeed it took longer. About 15 minutes after you paid by cash and left the restaurant, the problem was apparently fixed and we could process payments by cards again. Fantastic, however too late to process your payment.
Fortunately, there were only four tables facing inconvenience including yours.
Fortunately, these other guests paid with cash and they took the incident rather positive.
 
I do have to thank you for understanding that were not able to process the payment and I very much regret that you have to write a negative review.
 
I felt really bad and that is why I apologised to you and I apologise once again for the problem.
I am pretty certain that I apologise for the inconvenience of not able to charge your card on the spot, plus for the fact that we have to let you go out to withdraw money from the ATM.
 
Certainly service charge is added to bill, only 5%, and it is not 10% as you mentioned. The 10% is the VAT.

I am a bit confused by your comments us failing to provide premium service. Since there was this problem, I have the feeling that we offered several services, I would assume as premium.
Since you had to wait, I offered if we could get you any tea, coffee or after dinner drink, of course on us.
Also, after you paid, I offered to call a Grab Taxi or Uber Taxi at our expense after you paid to bring you back to the hotel or anywhere else you wished to go.
However, both offers were declined by you. (These offers would have, by the way, ended up more than a 5% or 10% deduction.)
Regretfully, I did have to ask you to take money from the ATM, however I did let our Assistant Manager Tâm go with you to walk to the closest ATM machine, which is just about 150 metres from the restaurant, a two-minute walk. Initially you insisted on going alone. As a service, I assume it was easier and faster to have Tâm with you get to the machines quicker. The three machines you tried are all on the same corner of the street, in a 15 metre radius of each one another.
Unlucky you were asking to withdraw money from a ATM machine of VietComBank, the very exact bank that had a malfunction (which is by the way located further way from our restaurant). I am of course not sure; however, I could guess that their ATM machines would have been affected by the interruption too. We could have brought you over, however I hope you will agree with me that it makes sense that we did not take that risk.
Your point of security and suspicion of quality of ATM machines in Vietnam is, in my perception, out of context for a review of our restaurant. Furthermore, the ATM machines and the hectic of traffic on the streets would still have been functioning the same when you would have been able to pay by card, that does not change, the traffic was the same when you arrived and will always be the same.
Indeed, there is a fee to take money out of the ATM, I am sorry for that, but that would have been the case as well when you take money out to pay the rest of your expenses in Vietnam, since credit cards are not accepted everywhere.
 
After this incident we are considering to change the bank, there are indeed other options. But that would mean as well that we have to give up to acceptance of the AMEX card, since most banks in Vietnam do not accept AMEX cards and VietComBank is one of the few that does. But, for sure, we are considering. We have received information from other banks here in the office already.
 
All in all, I really regret the inconvenience, and apologise again. I appreciate your feedback; it is your full right to write a review, I would just appreciate it very much if you write it in a fair light. It would have been nice to reflect the incident in a reasonable and realistic way. We offered services to apologise and for making matters easier, however I regret that is was not what you hoped for and consider we failed.
 
Kind regards,
Germ

Exceptional experience!
Dec 2016 • Family
Noir is located down an alleyway that runs off Hai Ba Trung. There is a Tous Les Jour (TLJ) diagonally across the road from Saigon Square on Hai Ba Trung - spot the TLJ cafe/bakery and the laneway is on the right of TLJ if you're facing away from the road. Noir is located at the very end of the lane way. 

A great concept and truly an experience that brings to mind simple things we take for granted daily, like the use of our sight. 

The food was wonderful and the sensation of not knowing what you're eating makes you feel a little adventurous. The staff ask before you dine whether you have any allergies to particular foods. 

We chose the West menu and it was delicious! It was fun trying to guess what you were eating and the 3 course meal was more than generous as we were all very satisfied. 

The next time I return, I will try the East menu! A vegetarian menu is also on offer although it is recommended that the whole table choose the same set menu - East, West or Vegetarian option. Really wonderful experience and the staff were all so lovely, each and every one of them.

Definitely worth a visit
May 2016 • Couples
This was a fun and interesting evening. Although it cost more than your average meal in Ho Chi Minh City, it still comes in at about half the price of a similar experience in other parts of the world (the UK especially).

Basically, you eat a meal in the dark and have to try to guess what it is that you've eaten. All of the waiters there are blind, except for one young man who is deaf (he deals with customers in the light part of the restaurant). 

We met the owner who is Swedish and this seems to be a real passion of his, which comes out in the ambiance and the food. When you go in you can pick with an Eastern or Western menu (we picked the Eastern one). They then explain a bit about how the evening will work and they get you to play a game with a blindfold to ease you in to eating in the dark. You get led into a room and the waiters explain where everything is and how to eat your food.

The food was good, although not all to my taste. It reinforced that I really do not like clams or tamarind! After you've finished eating they get you to guess what was in each meal and we were pretty much wrong about everything!

Great experience and worth the price.

Fine dining in the dark

This place is absolutely incredible, had some downtime in Ho Chi Minh city & decided to check out a few reviews on where to eat!! 

"Noir" came up as number 1....but there a catch! 

We were greeted at the door by several very friendly waiters of whom are either blind or deaf. 

We were seated at the entrance & offered a drink & briefed on what we are to expect from the evening! 

Noir is a restaurant that provides fine dining completely in the dark. No candles or dim lighting but completely pitch black..strange concept to understand until it's experienced! 

Before we were led into the pitch black dining room, we were presented with a menu & decided on the eastern degustation. We were then given a surprise game of trying to match some shapes and objects while blindfolded, this is actually a quick useful task to gather our senses of what was to come...dining in complete darkness. 

We then had to surrender phones & was greeted by our waiter for the night! 

We were politely led into the dining room & seated & within several minutes each course was presented. Like typical fine service we were told what fish to eat in succession, the notion of eating delicious food without fully knowing the dish is actually quiet fun. 

After each course was finished the waiter explained each meal in brief detail. 

The dining experience only lasts up to 40 mins due to the set courses which is perfect timing given the setting. 

After dinner was finished we were escorted back to the common area of the restaurant & to our delight were shown detailed images of each course. 

Overall this was a completely unique experience, well priced with fantastic food & service. 

Highly recommend!

reviews.review_text:

Delicious and engaging!!
Nov 2016 • Couples
This is an absolute must for anyone visiting Saigon!!

From the moment they welcome you into the restaurant you feel excited and interested in what you're about to experience. A welcome drink greets you, along with a blindfolded game to understand how you'll feel your way around the dinner table in the dark. You are given a thorough explanation of what to expect, and told the dark may be overwhelming but to keep calm and soon you'll adjust.

You're led to the dining room where you meet the wait staff who will be serving you and she leads you up the stairs into the dark - with your hands on her shoulders to lead the way.

The wait staff are blind, and there are deaf/mute people who are employed here as well. You're told it's difficult for them to find work in the city and this beautiful restaurant provides opportunities that might not otherwise present themselves for these amazing people.

Our waitress, Thu, is incredible. She brings the dishes to the table and you take your time experiencing 3-4 dishes per course, taking in the flavours and the textures in a way you've never before experienced.

Making conversation is different. You're told to keep your voice down as your automatic reaction to the void of the darkness is to raise your voice, somehow compensating for your lack of sight. The other diners are told the same, so the room has an energy of a typical dining room, with music playing, keeping everything quite energetic despite the natural response to be a bit sleepy.

I won't ruin the experience by revealing any of the dishes, as half the fun is guessing what you've just eaten, but I will say that as a picky Western eater there was nothing that upset me on the Eastern menu, and I was so glad to have made the choice to step outside my comfort zone.

After the meal they lead you back downstairs and give you time for your eyes to adjust to the light. They show you all the dishes you just ate and answer any questions you might have about the experience. 

With 2 Eastern menus and a cocktail each, we paid 1,600,000 VND (approx $70 USD) altogether for the 2 of us and I have to say it was well worth it. You would easily pay double for an experience like this back home. 

They're opening a new concept restaurant in December called blanc, in the same complex focused on deaf/mute staff. My understanding is that they'll teach you sign to order meals and communicate with your wait staff.

They've certainly tapped into something really special and I can't recommend this enough. This was an absolute highlight of my time in Saigon.

Thank you to all the wonderful staff at noir!!

Experience you will not soon forget
Nov 2016 • Business
If you're the wolf it down, pay the bill, and get on with it, you will not like Noir. If you are one of those types that 'doesn't want all the foolin around' when you just want to eat, you will not lik Noir. If you need your phone on the table or glued to your hand, you will not like Noir. If you.. well you get the point. This is an experience that manages to accomplish some tasks not easily done.

First, in the dark means just that. Surrender any light emitting device including phones, watches, lighters, etc. They lock them up, give you the key to the box and for the paranoid, suck it up or leave the phone in the hotel safe. 

Second, pick the opposite of where you're from. They have east or west selection. That's all you are told at the beginning. You will be getting 11 (if I remember right) tasting menu selections done in three courses, starter, main, dessert. 

Third, experience it. Really. You will be experiencing this from a couple of perspectives. The total darkness is 100% what it feels like to be blind. Blind like the very wait staff that is serving you. Within 10 minutes of being escorted, like a blind person, to your table, you will begin to pick up how quickly your hearing stops filtering out sound rather your brain begins to process it on a much more precise level. It something to experience.

There is the experience of the food. Having not only no idea and having no visual clues, you rely on your sense of taste. You really will taste and process what you are eating (eat slow) in a way that allows your sense of taste to overrule visual clues or many other 'I've heard that...' type prejudices you have in your head. It's truly an awakening of how the whole taste, smell, texture, etc. is supposed to operate. 

The food is very good. "Safe choices" meaning that after you are escorted back to the light, seated for tea, and have the chance to review what you eat, you won't be screaming "I ate that!!!" rather you will have a true appreciation for the meal.

This was an outstanding experience, very good food, excellent staff, and crazy reasonable price. Highly recommended.

This was the most interesting dinning experience I have had to date. Such an amazing, rewarding, humble learning experience and, lets not forget, dinner! My girlfriend took me here as something to do that was out of the ordinary on a Friday night. She nailed it! 

The greeting was wonderful. A drink, some blindfolds and few games to help release the idea and need of sight. An icebreaker comforting any anxiety or strange thoughts of what will happen next. This excited me. I was sold already. After a few words with other future diners, we were lead into the dinning room and instructed to place our hands on our waiters shoulders. He then led us in and helped us with organization of the table and really let us explore on our own occasionally checking in to make sure all was going well! Everyone around us seemed to have the same experience. Truly fantastic. Very unique. Delicious food. Strange atmosphere. Incredibly positive vibes. 

They offer an Eastern, Western and Veggie menu. We went vegan and all dishes were a success! The menu changes every 3 months - so...already counting down the days. 

Also, all waiters are blind. This was the coolest part. It was nice to step into their world and experience the world in their shoes. It was nice to know jobs like this exist. Our waiter seemed so happy and made me feel so happy.

A big thanks to the people that made this happen. Its a WIN WIN WIN situation and I am honored to have taken part. See you next time!

Special Charity Event - Menu created by Chef Christine Ha
Oct 2016 • Business
Christine Ha, the third season winner of the show MasterChef, created the menu for our meal last night and a portion of the proceeds went to a charity supported by Christine. We knew that the menu would be delicious, but it was actually absolutely brilliant.

When we arrive, we were ushered into the front sitting area where we were greeted by a staff member who asked what kind of welcome beverage we wanted: alcoholic or non-alcoholic. Once we made our selections, she returned with our beverages and a game to orient us to the darkness. She provided blindfolds and we had to put various shaped wooden blocks into the correct position on the puzzle board. Once we were done with the puzzle, we were escorted to the locker area where we deposited our bags, watches and phones. We were then greeted by a blind waiter (who was so super accommodating and sweet) who took us into the dining area by holding on to his shoulders.

Once in the dining area, it is dark. Not a bit dark, more like total overwhelming darkness. It is absolutely amazing, because your other senses do become keener, especially sensitivity to sound. During each course, we couldn't help but wonder what we were eating in the darkness. However, every course was divine. 

After the dining experience, were escorted out and taken to the locker areas to retrieve our belongings. Once we had our bags, we were escorted to an area where we reviewed photos of each course on an iPad with a staff member. The menu was exquisite and the photos were beautiful. We enjoyed hokkaido clam, mango salad with beef jerky, beef, chicken with masala, duck with shallot and berry reduction, prawn consomme, tomato soup with parmesan croutons, tuna, chocolate panna cotta, pumpkin cheesecake, calamansi sherbert and more. 

It was definitely worth the 780K VND because the meal was everything we hoped for. The service was impeccable, the food was divine and the experience was amazing. Dining in the dark is definitely new for me, but I hope to experience it again.

I highly recommend this experience.

Wow, I can't recommend this fabulous place enough!! 
My boyfriend and I visited on a short weekend trip to Ho Chi Minh and I'm so thrilled we included it in our visit.
Everything about the restaurant, the meal and the service was 5*!

I was a little apprehensive about a meal in the dark. I didn't understand how it would work. 
All my doubts and concerns were put to rest as soon as we arrived. 

Before your meal, you are seated in a lovely waiting area/bar. 
The staff make every effort to make you feel so comfortable and welcome, plus they really do a good job of explaining how the meal works. I think this really settles your doubts. 

We had a delicious welcome drink and the staff brought over games to play. The games included wearing a blindfold, which was a nice little introduction to 'the darkness'.

Before you enter the dark dining area, we were introduced to our waiter for the evening. All of the waiters are blind or sight impaired, which immediately gives the whole experience much deeper meaning. It's a chance to step into their world for awhile and rely on your other senses for the evening.
Our waiter was called Dan or 'Tan' and he was fantastic! 

When you first enter the dark dining area, it is very overwhelming. 
I have never really experienced complete darkness like it. 
I have to admit, I was a little unsure about the total blackness at first. 
It takes about 5 minutes to get used to your surroundings and the noise, but after adjusting to not being able to see anything, you begin to realise just how much you can enjoy all your other senses! 

I don't think I will say much more about the meal itself because it all speaks for itself. 
I guess my review here focuses on the lead up to the dining experience because I don't want to give too much away about the meal itself... The surprise was all part of the enjoyment! 

All I can really say about the food is it definitely does not disappoint!
It was completely delicious from start to finish.
The darkness was actually a delightful way to enjoy the food and company... and it was so refreshing to spend time away from phones and gadgets!! 

The whole experience was very memorable indeed.
Not only do you come away feeling thoroughly impressed by the flavours and tastes of the wonderful menu, but you come back out into the light with absolute appreciation for your eyesight. 
The experience definitely heightens and stimulates all your senses, but mostly it reminds you that your eyesight is never something we should take for granted!

Concept Wasn't for Me, But...
Sep 2016 • Couples
This is a super long review, but I've thought a lot about it. Overall, I think they're doing a good job with the concept. And from the other reviews, it's clear that lots of other people are enjoying it--that's great.

Another plus is that they've come up with a creative and mostly delicious vegetarian menu, which is not always the case. One of the staff mentioned that they change several times per year, and this particular menu had only been in rotation for one week.

Overall, I felt like the emphasis was on the novelty rather than the meal itself. For example, when I say the food was "mostly" delicious--there were definitely moments where it seemed that the point of the dish was to fool you into trying to figure out what was in it, rather than actually being delicious. I felt that the meal could have used a few simpler dishes for contrast...some of it seemed a bit "muddy".

Neither my partner nor I found it enjoyable being in the dining area itself--actually, we both commented that it seemed like we were rushing through the meal just to get through it. That's mostly a comment on the concept rather than the quality of the restaurant.

Two things I think they could definitely do better. 1) It is really cacophonous in the dining area, and feels like you're right on top of the other diners. Other senses are heightened in the dark, I understand, but it seems like they should be able to add some additional acoustic panels or something. 

2) It was absolutely freezing in there! And again, heightened senses, but that's a problem to solve, not an excuse to make. Definitely part of the reason I was rushing through. Near the end of the meal I heard someone else complain about the cold, and their server offered them a scarf....if you know this is a problem, why not offer that to every diner at the beginning of the meal? Or attach one to the back of the chair?

After the meal, they'll show you photos of what you ate and explain all of the dishes in the lobby. The presentation is beautiful, and we were again left wishing that we had just plain seen the food.

I wonder what the experience would be like if instead of serving very complicated, tricky dishes, they served more familiar dishes (even just Vietnamese, maybe), done very well. It would be really interesting to see how a dish you already know is experienced differently without one sense. And perhaps with more of a focus on understanding and connection to people with visual impairments? The servers were blind, and some other staff were deaf, which I appreciate...but I think the overall experience would be a lot more meaningful with a larger connection to the particular challenges and possibilities that people with disabilities in Vietnam experience. I won't go back for something that's just a trend/novelty, but I would go back for good food situated within some larger meaningful context.

One other note. I think the concept might be more enjoyable in a group rather than just a couple--we saw several families, and I can imagine it being more fun with a group of friends. Just a guess.

The worst
Sep 2016 • Couples
I never had this awful service experience in my intire life as I am the one who also work in this industry.

It was our first exciting experience of dining in the dark. We started the dining, served by lovely girl Xuan and everything was good. 

When we had our main course, a group of people came and sitting next to us. That the guests at the other table were loud. Yes, there is absolutely no need to raise the voice in the dark dining room and I do understand hearing does become sharper in the dark. That is also why manger/supervisor need to ask all of their diners to be considerate with the other diners in the dining room.- They didn't mention to us at the Lounge before we started the dining. (We just learnt from their website)

We understood the situation and tried to continue but I had to cover my ears with my hands more than five minutes. It seemed no one controlled the voice level and we couldn't stand it. 

We've been asked to finish our course to upstairs by one of the lady staff but we already lost our appetite and said No.

We felt so sorry to Xuan, our server. I told her it was not her fault. I thought it was me and I wasn't upset, until I met the manager, Germ.

About 5 minutes later, I saw him walked into the Lounge and he talked with the lady who suggested us to dine upstairs.

A few minutes later, he came and said,
"How was it?" - seriously????? "How was it?"
I thought he was not informed anything about us. I tried to tell him the situation, then he cut my story and started to explain (rather teach) us. 

What I wanted to hear was not all the ctrl+c & ctrl+v answers as you may see on all the answers for negative reviews.

Yes, my drinks been off from my bill which I didn't even ask for. And yes, I had appology emails later on (same ctrl+c & ctrl+v things-wonder they even read before sent to me???) but I never get simple "SORRY" in that place where I suppose to hear. 

I tried to leave a review on that night but I decided not. Because it could be very emotional and now it is been a week. I still feel like to leave a review for their further future. 

To the owner,
Your concept is good and Team is extra ordinary. Just spend more time to take care of customers on site -not on the Web. I read every single reviews of yours and I think you sure know what is the main problem is. And one more thing, the people who treats the customers like this, how would he treat his people?
Read more
Written September 9, 2016
Germ D
Dear Mrs Lee,
Thank you and your husband very much for visiting our restaurant a little while ago.
I am pleased that you like the concept and appreciate the employment of our blind and visually impaired staff.
It is with regret that we have to read your negative comments and you feel your dinner at our restaurant was the worst in your life. I am very sorry to hear that.

We are very much aware that it is impossible, as much as we care, to please all of the people, all of the time.
I am very sad to see you posted this review, especially after you and your husband already posted each a review on google.

The team and I understand that loud voices in the dining room can be quiet frustrating and intrusive. We are definitely aware off that.
• That is why we have sound absorbing material installed on the wall and ceiling.
• In the briefing for every guest before entering the dining room we do inform people not to speak louder and to be considerate with the other diners in the room. We speak to every guest, every time, as per very strict standards. And hope to rely on the consideration of all guests.
• After your comments to Ms Xuan we offered to change your table to a different room, or continue the desserts in the lit part of the restaurant. Unfortunately, you did decline.
• As a token of good will, I did take of the wines off your bill and we did not charge you for the dessert and matching wine you did not have. I do not think we need your permission for that, as said a token of good will. Sad to hear you do not appreciate this offer.
• I believe, in our conversation we had after dinner I did apologise and indeed did explain. I am sorry to hear if you felt it as teaching. I had the need to explain, since this is such a different dining experience. And most of the people are rather considerate and understanding. 
• Plus both my partner and I sent several emails to apologise and asking for feedback to serve you and other guest better in the future, to which we did not get a response, unless I have missed it. We did reach out, sadly it is not appreciated.

If one is not being considerate with the other diners in the room, that is a case of manners, and that is indeed frustrating, and it is terrible if it affects the dining experience of other guests. Again, it is a combination of our sense of hearing becoming sharper, plus most of our guests are excited and that shows if having them to use loud voices. Again, there is truly no need for that. Even whispering would suffice. Again, this is not blaming, it is explaining. 
We did luckily did not receive other complaints that night. Also the service staff did mention this table not being louder than the average guest.
It is truly a pity, though, it affected your dining experience in a bad way. We see it as a challenge to make sure for each and every guests we are able to provide a great experience. It is sad, it did not work out in your situation, and that does hurt. We failed making you happy.

Of course the answers on the web and the personal conversations are similar, since there is not a different way. It is both about the dining experience guests have.
As you mentioned you have read all the reviews, you may have seen that each and every one is different and personalised. Sad that you have to take such a personal negative approach.

Having said all that, we do respect every guest’s feedback, even if it negative. We can learn from it, we understand our guests better, where possible and realistic.
Once again, both my partner and I regret that we were not able to give you a great evening. I hope it is a just a cause of misunderstanding. I know you may never come back, and I understand and respect that, however we do like to have the opportunity to welcome you back and show we do take care of our guests, as most of guest do appreciate,
Kind regards,
Germ

Taste Bud Delight
Aug 2016 • Family
Not being enamoured of the dark when my family suggested Noir I was somewhat reluctant about eating what I couldn't see but went along the way you do for family. Oh boy was I wrong. The intention of the restaurant is to take away your preconceived likes and dislikes and test your taste buds with new experiences. They quiz you first about allergies then tell you about their staff who are all either deaf or blind and/or disabled in some way. In a city like HCM that's an incredibly difficult life and their staff get jobs not available elsewhere. Big plus. Our waiter Bao was blind and so we entered his dark world. No phones or even watches that light up were allowed. You have no clue what you're going to eat but then after each course they challenge you to identify what it was - next to no hope! Bao's service was excellent and done with an understanding of what you are experiencing. Suffice to say that feeling your way to the food then letting your taste buds work without your eyes ends with a superb meal at a reasonable cost and best of all a completely different experience which forces you to appreciate what you normally take for granted. If you get the chance jump at it. You will not regret it.

Superb - a must-go for any trip to HCMC
Sep 2016 • Solo
This was my first visit to Noir and I was very impressed with this social enterprise. Noir employs people who are blind, partially impaired as well as mute and hard of hearing and empowers them by giving them essential work experience.

I dined alone and was the only one at the restaurant (at least I think I was) for the 6pm sitting. The experience started with a free cocktail followed by a puzzle game you play in blind-fold. You are presented with a choice in menus (West, East or Veggie) although the specific items are not disclosed. A drinks and wine list is also provided. 

Once your belongings are safely locked away, you are guided up to the restaurant by your waiter. The courses are served fairly quickly - the wait between courses was very short (perhaps because I was dining alone) but I entered the restaurant at 6pm and left at 7pm - including the briefing and games etc. The food was good although I must admit not Michelin standard by any means. I was served 11 dishes in total - 4 starters, 4 mains and 3 desserts. The price is very reasonable compared to western standards - I paid approx £20 which is cheap for the quality and range offered. 

I can't say my other senses were heighted as a result of being in the dark - and managed to guess most of the dishes correctly. But the service was impeccable and Sung my waitress spoke excellent English and kept me at ease throughout the sitting.

Very enjoyable experience and definitely one that I will remember!

He was so understanding that this would be a new experience and brought and guided us with care. He was so attentive to us, had some chats with us about our life and his but in a subtle way, how a waiter should. 

I won't go into the food. I'd rather leave it as a surprise but there were lots of different things served. Amazing mouthwatering food from the western menu. 

When we finished we were taken outside to reception and a really nice man showed us pictures of what we had. He went into some detail of what the restaurant is about. It seems like there is so much more to it than serving food. That these employees are really cared about which is nice to see in any job. 

The restaurant reception and bar is stunning and super clean and so was the toilet which I loved. The outside area has lovely chairs to sit on.

Food is good, but over charged
Jul 2016 • Business
I enjoyed their idea dishes, however, if you weight the location, decorations, cost with the charge, it is too much expensive. As to eating in the dark, it is a interesting experience, but I more enjoy to see what I eat , for me, it is a part of taste. Anyway, no harm to give it a try.
Written July 24, 2016
Germ D
Dear Ann,
Thank you for having dinner at Noir. Dining in the Dark and for sharing your opinion on this site.
I am pleased that you liked the dinner and the food. Pity to hear that you feel the price is too high. There are indeed plenty of cheap eating options in HCMC and Vietnam, however there are also plenty of restaurants that charge way more. We do feel however that we charge a very fair price for the products and services we offer. It is sad as well that you feel the location and the decoration are not up to your expectations. We did actually receive many positive comments on the location – in that sense of being quietly located at the end of the alley, and we are still in District 1 , quite central though – and on the decoration – in that sense that one feels the lounge and the decoration is cosy and tasteful. Of course tastes differ. And in the dark dining room is no decoration at all naturally.
Everybody does eat with one’s eyes, our sight is very dominant, it accounts fro 70% of our five senses. Once having a meal in the dark the “other” senses heighten and one is more focussed on the taste and smell and that makes a dinner interesting, because suddenly you notice how difficult it actually is to identify the different ingredients. It helps of course to come to our restaurant open-minded and we do hope that from now on you “see” your meals in a different light. 
Thank you for the recommending words and maybe we do have the opportunity to welcome you back again,
Kind regards,
Germ

Great food and concept
Jul 2016 • Friends
Decided to eat there right before flying off and it was definitely a good decision. 

When we arrived we were greeted with drinks and a little short game to test our senses. After which we led to a dark room and lunch was served there. And because it was pitched dark we were introduced to our food at the reception area after we finished the session.

Service 
Service was good and responsive, the staff were conversant in English and were able to give us clear instructions on what we needed to do. What was amazing was how even though some of the staff were visually challenged, there were still able to provide us with excellent service. To put it simply they were really professional. 

Food
We decided to go for the Asian set and it did not disappoint, the food was delicious and the flavors were a mix of the various Asian cuisines they don't just stop at Vietnamese; we even had a dish which was Malaysian laksa flavored (a kind of curry).

Would definitely recommend this to travelers in HCM city. Definitely worth the money and the money goes a long way to help those working there. Go and support this social enterprise and dine for a cause.

Diana M
Australia44 contributions

Best experience ever!
Jul 2016 • Family
When I read about Noir on TripAdvisor I was impressed with all the comments and it made me wonder if it could live up to the magnificent reviews. However I was travelling with my mum and she was extremely hesitant about it, she kept on arguing against the whole experience about eating in the dark in a foreign country. Regardless I made a booking for two on our last night in Ho Chi Minh, due to Noir's location (at the end of a small road) mum's reluctance continued. Their waiting room is very inviting and all the staff are lovely. Once we were presented to our waiter and guided to our table mum's attitude changed completely, the food was delicious and rather surprising, what I thought for certain was something ended up being a completely different thing. Noir goes beyond providing customers with delicious food, this place is all about the experience as a whole, it invites customers to surrender vision for the curse of the meal and rely only on touch, smell and sound and I can guarantee it is worth it. The experience was spectacular, it made us appreciate how lucky we are. at the end of the meal, our visit to Noir become mum's best experience of our whole trip. Do not let reluctance deprived you from what could be a wonderful evening. Book for an early table before their dinner rush hour, this will allow you to enjoy the meal better and avoid possible customers who tend to get loud in the dark
Read more
Written July 24, 2016
Germ D
Dear Diana,
Thank you very much for your kind review, and it was certainly a pleasure to welcome you and your mother.
At our restaurant we are very proud of our service and it is always a pleasure to know we achieved our goal: providing a unique experience to our guests and meet every guest’s expectations. I am extremely glad that your mother considered her dinner at Noir. Dining in the Dark as the best during her trip, especially since, as you mentioned, was rather reluctant.
The thing is that we are still a restaurant, our guests come with expectations and the concept of dining in the dark should stand in the way, we still have to make sure our guest are being served excellent dishes with the best service possible. 
It does indeed make you realise how important our eyes are and how much we are actually depended on them. We tend to overlook and take our senses for granted, but here at Noir. Dining in the Dark we learn how to appreciate them. As the menus are not disclosed beforehand and no one is able to see while dining at our restaurant, we want to ensure our diner feel comfortable and confident as they enjoy their dinner. So, our guides are trained to explain the table setting, how each course is laid out and where to begin. 
Thank you once again for the kind words and it would be a delight to welcome you back once your travels bring you back to Vietnam,
Kind regards,
Germ

Great Experience
Jul 2016
We went to noir as a group of 8 people including 4 adults and 4 children. The waiters/waitresses were very welcoming and organized to make sure everything went as planned. We are first greeted by the waiters that give us a welcome drink and a menu that does not say what we will eat but a choice between east, west and vegetarian three course set menu. We opted to all take the east menu to try to guess the food and share experiences. We then played a blind folded matching game to gauge our senses after which they took us inside a pitch black dining area. Several of the employees are disabled and our waitress Swan was blind. At first we felt lost regarding placement of food/cutlery then you get used to it and actually it comes second nature. Overall a good experience that heightens your senses of taste and hearing and it was an interesting game to guess food and ingredients. After we are done, the owner showed us the menu and it was fun to find out what we got right/wrong. The experience overall was great and we congratulate owners on the place. Food is kind of bland though and could be improved.

Great concept and support for the handicapped, but don't come here for the food

We decided to eat here after reading all the wonderful reviews on trip advisor. We weren't completely disappointed - the staff were phenomenal and we love the concept of eating in darkness. Sadly, the food let it down completely. It was bland, tasteless and perhaps even stale? We did discuss the freshness of the food with the staff afterwards and were told it was fresh, full stop. Regardless of that, it didn't taste fresh.

I don't mean to be harsh but this restaurant is surviving on the basis of the concept and its support for the handicapped, not the food. Next time, we will $100 (for two!!!) to charity and eat somewhere cheaper and tastier.

Written July 11, 2016
Germ D
Dear Emma,
Thank you for your review and for choosing our restaurant for dinner. 
I am grateful you welcome the concept and the blind and visually impaired staff in our service team. I am glad that you found the staff phenomenal and like the experience of eating in the dark.

The team and I are saddened and shocked though that you feel the food is not good/not fresh. We are indeed a restaurant and want to stay miles away from novelty or gimmick feeling. That is why we place so much effort on the food and service. It is a restaurant for you as guest and also for the blind staff, for them it is proper employment. Of course there is no light in the dining room and there is indeed blind and visually impaired staff, however that should not take away from an actual restaurant experience, we cannot permit ourselves to compromise on the restaurant, the service and the food, exactly as you say. In fact we are very proud of our kitchen team.

All feedback is very much appreciated and we do value very much what our guests say, even though it is subjective to say personal sometimes. Thank you very much for addressing the freshness with the staff straight after dinner. That is helpful, fair and honest, however, I must agree with the staff telling you that the food is fresh, indeed full stop.
It is entirely not possible in our concept and kitchen operation that food cannot be fresh, let me attempt to explain: 
- First of all we are a restaurant were guests cannot see the food, so we have to make sure all the dishes are very much enjoyed by our guests, very basic things here are freshness and safety. After that of course we need to make sure the dishes are prepared nicely and have good taste and smell. Our Chef and her team are carefully selecting and preparing the dishes in the morning for dinner service. We only work with quality ingredients from certified suppliers. The preparation of the food has to follow our standard of operations and strict guidelines. The team loves the preparation of slow-cooking and sous-vide. They really take the time for it.
- Secondly we do only have two main set menus East and West with very small stock of dishes and together a very high turn-over of the ingredients, commonly there is no food left over for the next days. 
- Thirdly all of our staffs have worked for many years in hospitality and we do love our jobs, there is a lot of integrity in our team. It would not even pop to our minds to have not fresh food being served. There is a lot of commitment.

It is indeed rather regretful that you felt the food is not fresh and we are sorry to hear we could not please you with the dishes served.

If you need any further discussion or verify this case, please email me directly: germ@noirdininginthedark.com or call at +84 9 8663 2525.
Again, it would be a pleasure to welcome you back to assure you we do have great commitment to food quality and freshness. Hopefully upon your next visit we have the opportunity to regain your confidence, we are looking forward to it,
Kind regards,
Germ

My wife and I visited this as part of our quick stopover in Vietnam. Not the cheapest of things to be doing in South East Asia, but what an experience! If you have a spare night, and you don't know what to do - DO THIS!

Like many of you, we pondered on what to do in HCMC by looking over Tripadvisor. The both of us love our food, but more importantly, the experience that came with dining.

The experience itself was quite surreal. Be prepared that most taxi drivers don't know this location, and we ended up having to walk a little as we were dropped off approximately 300m from the actual location itself. 

The wait staff were excellent - and we started our night off with a game of fit the blocks, blindfolded...which was not too hard for me, but my wife did take a while to get the hang of it.

We were led by a beautiful, visually impaired waitress, who was fluent in English and had an awesome sense of humour. We chose the East menu, and our tastebuds were in for an awakening.

We were both led up a really dimly lit staircase, into an almost pitch black room. We were seated down, and in total darkness, we got to explore our utensils and tables. The food itself was really really good, although perhaps the portions were a tad small.

We managed to guess about 60% of the food that we ate, but we were honestly surprised at how much of a visual eater we both were.

The staff were excellent and friendly, and I love the fact that this establishment offers the physically disabled employment opportunities.

Recommend this restaurant for those who are looking for something different! Especially for group dinners!

Sarah K

0
Time flew as we ate in the dark
Jun 2016
These restaurants are popping up all over the world but Noir was my first experience in a eat-in-the-dark restaurant.

You are welcomed at the front by a friendly maitre de who brings you your choice of a surprise alcoholic or non-alcoholic drink.

And your education begins. You are asked to guess the ingredients. Of course you have a clue because of the colour of the drink. Soon you will only have taste and smell to guide you.

You are given a choice of Eastern, Western or Vegetarian menus and a wine choice as well (we chose surprise wines and Eastern)

Then we were given a child's shape puzzle and another staff member - this one deaf and mute - showed us how we would put on a blindfold and put the correct shapes into the puzzle board.

(I was pleased to beat my husband in this task!)

This was going to stand us in good stead shortly.

We were asked to remove any light emitting devices and place in a locker. Off went the fitbit and goodbye phone!

We then went to the dark restaurant and were introduced to our waiter Toh who was completely blind.

I put my hands on her shoulders and my husband put his on mine and we followed her into the restaurant.

It was pitch black inside. 

The only thing I could see was a tiny red light up at the ceiling. A comfort light perhaps. I couldn't see my hand in front of my face.

Toh told us where things were and brought out the first course.

You got four dishes per course and they were arranged on a tray with holes - like the puzzle. You were asked to eat the courses in order.

Toh was charming and friendly and kept up an amusing banter as she served our food.

We found that we lost time while in the restaurant. When we came out it was much later than we expected.

Afterwards our host took us through what we had eaten and we were asked to guess what we ate.

I was pretty pleased to have picked most flavours.

What I loved about the food was the mixture in texture and tastes, hot and cold. The food really had your brain working!

We learned while we were there that the restaurant employs about 11 blind or mostly blind people and that they are planning to open a deaf restaurant shortly where you can only communicate through sign language.

I think that would also be very interesting to try.

Don't think that this is just a feel good experience supporting people with disabilities; the food is excellent!

An Incredible Experience

My husband and I had dinner at Noir during our stay in Ho Chi Minh City in April 2016. Having read so many wonderful reviews about this restaurant, I will admit my expectations were high. We were definitely not disappointed. It is somewhat difficult to accurately describe the experience, so I encourage people who are sitting on the fence about it to just do it, you will not regret it. After being served a welcome drink on arrival, we were blind folded and instructed to complete some puzzles to get us in the right mindset for dinner. We were shown to our table by our waiter, the darkness is a little overwhelming at first, but you get used to it. I really liked how our waiter helped us work out where everything on the table was - so there weren't any accidents involving spilled drinks! We both went for the Traditional Vietnamese menu and the food was lovely, the whole 'guessing game' that evolves is equally as fun. Each course generally comprised of 4 small dishes served in small bowls - I felt that this made eating the food a lot easier. After finishing our 3 courses, we were shown back out of the dining room where we were debriefed by our host who went through each dish we ate, the philosophy and the ingredients. Overall, it is a very interesting, unique experience that we would highly recommend.

Amazing and Memorable Experience
May 2016 • Friends
First time trying this out. Dining in the dark. 
Didn't know what to expect. Upon arrival, we were familiarized by playing a game that would help us out during the dinner. 
Staff were very patient and friendly explaining how the whole concept of dining in the dark would work....calming all the various anxieties that we had. 

After the little game and knowing how to 'cope' with dining in the dark, we were led upstairs to the dining area. this is where it gets pitched black. You can't even see your own fingers in front of you!

Starters, mains and desserts were served. Each course had mini dishes (which the game we played earlier helped). Food was absolutely amazing. Not being able to see your food really opens up your senses. 

It'll take a bit of time to adjust to the fact that your eyes are opened but yet you don't see anything. The whole dining experience lasted about an hour for me and my friends. Our server (and all servers working there) were vision impaired and was really friendly. 

It is a highly recommended activity and you'll have no regrets trying this. Do make reservations early as places may run out quick especially during weekends. The entrance to this place is through a street off the main street. Just walk all the way to the end.

Great experience at a high price
Apr 2016 • Couples
Noir's claim to fame is dining in complete darkness, so you're paying for the experience more than for the food. Both were top-notch: our server spoke decent English and was extremely pleasant, the food was fantastic and I was surprised how unique it was eating without my sight. My girlfriend, Lisa, and I ate together and chatted the whole time about the experience, making it much more enjoyable than it would have been otherwise. This is a great date experience.

The first thing I noticed about eating in the dark was how well I could navigate the table. With relatively little effort, I was always able to find my water, my silverware, and the bowl I was eating from. My second surprise was how terrible I was at guessing what I was eating - it was all delicious, but I was almost always wrong about what I had just eaten! Lisa was better at guessing than me. They go over everything with you at the end, which is a big part of what makes this worth your time. 

The eating experience, paired with a bit of fanfare before and after the meal, amounts to a great time. I'm very happy I chose to add this to my vacation. On the other hand, it's a steep price for Saigon and the portions aren't very large (I got a snack after our meal to fill me up), so I could see where others might find it wasn't worth the price tag. Also, I'm not sure if they ever book multiple groups in the same area, but I wouldn't be nearly as excited about the experience if we hadn't been alone. They placed us at "table 7", but I never heard anyone but our server. 

I probably wouldn't go a second time, but I'm very glad I went for my first.

Written April 25, 2016
Germ D
Dear Phuong Vu,
Thank you or visiting our restaurant last year November for a corporate event. Thank you as well for leaving your feedback.
I am glad that you like the concept and appreciate the employment of blind and visually impaired staff. 
We are pretty shocked to read that you consider the food stale, it is entirely not possible in our concept & kitchen operation, let me attempt to explain: 
- First of all we are a restaurant were guests cannot see the food, so we have to make sure all the dishes are very much enjoyed by our guests, very basic things here are freshness and safety. After that of course we need to make sure the dishes are prepared nicely and have good taste and smell. Our Chef and her team are carefully selecting and preparing the dishes in the morning for dinner service. It has to follow our standard of operations and strict guidelines.
- Secondly we do only have two main set menus East and West with very small stock of dishes and together a very high turn-over of the ingredients, commonly there is no food left over for the next days. 
- Thirdly all of our staffs have worked for many years in hospitality and we do love our jobs, there is a lot of integrity in our team. It would not even pop to our minds to have stale food being served. There is a lot of commitment.

We do like processes where food is slow-cooked. We really take the time for it. It is quite hurting that you consider the food to be stale or not fresh as you say. The dish in particular is shredded pulled pork in a home-made BBQ sauce with crunchy baby potatoes, has been slow-cooked, marinated for two days and four hours roasted in the oven. We have used very fresh products for it, but the slow-cooking does not make it stale or not fresh. Actually the dish is very soft, it kind of melts in your mouth. Back in the time when this dish was in the menu, we have received a lot of positive comments on it. 
All feedback is very much appreciated and we do value very much what our guests say, even though it is subjective to say personal sometimes. However, like a machine or human being, we are all not perfect. If it would have happen to us, we would appreciate your constructive feedbacks right after dinner, not after 6 months. It would be helpful for us to review/inspect or investigate and make sure nothing will be similar happen again for next guests. If you need any further discussion or verify this case, please email me directly: germ@noirdininginthedark.com or call at +84 9 8663 2525.
Again, it would be a pleasure to have you come back to assure you we do have great commitment to food quality. Hopefully we have the opportunity to welcome you have to regain your confidence, we are looking forward to it,
Kind regards,

Image being blind - would you want to be blind from birth or go blind?? These were some of the questions that were asked by our ourselves on our night at Noir. This restaurant has so many plus's. It is set up to give blind people jobs - fantastic as there is a 95% unemployment rate for blind people in Vietnam. It gives you an experience that you may never have in your life again - when you get told it is dining in the dark that is an understatement - it is pitch black - very unusual sensation but well worth it. The food - this is a fine dining restaurant but in saying that the food is still fairly normal nothing too over the top - 4 tasting plates of entree, the same of main and then 3 desserts It is hard to describe that what you think you are eating may not be exactly. The staff accommodated our daughters needs of gluten free (due to being coeliac) perfectly - a big plus for her who was very paranoid of not being able to see what was being put in front of her and having to trust that her intolerance was being catered for properly. Our blind winter was wonderful - she couldn't have been more attentive and polite - well done. Being able to see what you have eaten on the ipad at the end of the evening is great - somethings totally amaze you and others you have identified. The cost per person was approximately $35 australian each - so not really expensive overall. Perfect English over the phone by the booking staff, Overall this is an experience well worth doing - would totally recommend to anyone visiting HCM.

EXQUISITE
Mar 2016 • Family
This place will pull on your heart strings as well as tantalise your taste buds in a unique gourmet dining experience.
Upon entering the premises you will be met by a mute young man who will request you to put on a blindfold before instructing you in an exercise you need to undertake to enhance your sense of touch to compensate for loss of your sense of sight when you go into the restaurant itself.
You are asked to select the eastern menu or the western menu and, having done so, you are led to and seated at your table by a young man who will be either totally blind or severely visually impaired. He will also be your waiter.
You will first have to surrender your watch and mobile phone and anything else that might possibly emit light in the pitch black of the restaurant.
Irrespective of whether you select the eastern or the western menu you will be served 11 dishes - 4 entrees, 4 mains and 3 desserts.
You will be served any wine or other drink you may have ordered (or may order during the course of the meal).
When it is all over the same waiter will lead you from the restaurant where you will be shown on an iPad precisely what you have eaten, having first been invited to try to identify the dishes on the basis of their texture and flavour.
The food is absolutely exquisite and whilst on the high side for Saigon in terms of price absolutely worth every cent and then some.
Alcohol is not cheap but nor is it so expensive that it should deter you from experiencing what is a dining extravaganza in a truly unique environment.
Absolutely not to be missed.

Good Experience
Mar 2016
This was to be our dinner of the trip for the two of us on our visit to Ho Chih Min City. We arrived early for our 6pm slot and they accommodated to bring our slot to 5.30pm. The place is not easily seen from the main road but we had Google Maps and that was a great help.

The restroom was clean and they clean it every time someone used it and replenished all towels etc. Impressive. We were seated in the lounge and served our inclusive cocktail and someone lead us through a before dinner game to get ourselves orientated to the dinner in the dark. Fumbling through, it was a taste of what was to come.

When we were done with our drink, we were given a briefing of what's to come and what to do/ not to do, then we kept our stuff in a locker (luminous watches, handphones, etc) and given the opportunity to visit the restroom again before dinner.

We chose the Western menu and were told that they change the menu once every three months. The staff was fabulous and our assigned dining assistant for dinner was great! We were lead into the dark room through a series of zig zags (used to cut out all light) and we were seated..with help of course. I won't go into detail the entire experience since one must find out and enjoy it for themselves save to say that it was enjoyable and in the entire meal, the discussion was mainly about what's in the 11 dishes served. Our early attempt to eat 'normally' failed and we ended up scooping food into our mouths off the bowls! Little things - simple tasks like toasting my wife with our glasses turned out to be funny events.

Food was ok but we think it was because we were not aided by our sight as otherwise it would definitely have tasted better. Familiar tastes turned out to be difficult to pinpoint. Even if you can guess the main ingredient, you would inevitably get things all wrong or all mixed up. You will find out what you ate and what the ingredients are when you are seated in the lounge again after dinner. Someone will go through it with you on an I-pad.

Lovely experience. We were told that the owners plan to open another dining hall upstairs where one would order food in an 'environment' where one cannot hear/speak. That would be interesting.

Worth the experience.

Hearing does become more sensitive and there are naturally more guests in the dining room. I am sorry to hear that other guests take away the special moment of eating in the dark. Sometimes, we wonder though, if people do really talk louder in the dark; do they really think it is needed to compensate the lack of sight by talking louder, or is it just that one is more focussed on hearing since you cannot see? Even in the light people can be loud, however we might not notice, since sight is so dominant.
Anyway, it is a pity that we could not give you the full enjoyment of dining in complete darkness.

Attending to Your Other Senses
Jul 2015 • Family
Black out dining is such an interesting experience. The whole concept is to focus on your other senses, because 70% of it comes from your vision. Upon entering the restaurant, you are seated in a waiting room with drinks and a fun, blind folded game to get you used to using your hands. Then, your menu preference is taken (from two choices), and you are given a secure locker for your belongings. You're then lead to the connecting building, and your server takes you to your table.

In the beginning, the experience is slightly unnerving due to the complete darkness. However, after you realize that you're not in a haunted walk through attraction, everything becomes fun! Our waiter was great at guiding us through our course, and the food was amazing. At the end of your meal, you are given a menu of pictures of what you have eaten. To keep things interesting, the menu is changed every few months.

A wonderful thing to note about this particular restaurant is that the owner hires visually impaired servers. I personally think it's such a pleasant thing to hear, considering finding employment in this situation can be rather difficult. I definitely would revisit in the future.
