A sensory experience like no other
Jan 2016 • Couples
We visited tonight and absolutely LOVED it. The service, food and experience as a whole is incredible. 

We were welcomed with a drink and a blindfolded game to get us used to the experience. You choose your menu out of eastern, western or vegetarian cuisine - we chose eastern and were not disappointed! 

You are lead into the dining room by a visually impaired staff member who is your server for the night. This is done by putting your hands on your servers shoulders and the person with you with their hands on your shoulders. 

Dinner is a three course meal and is made up of four dishes for starters and mains and three dishes for desert. It's constantly changing. The meals are done with the highest quality of culinary skill and you can tell. The meats are delectable and the flavours sing. Not being able to see heightens the experiences and makes the tastes feel colourful. 

If you're in Saigon, you must go here. We will be talking about this for months.

Jan 2016 • Couples
From start to finish it was an experience you will find hard to replicate. 

Met by the very welcoming staff, what lies ahead is all explained through words and games. Once you are ready and you have chosen between a western or Eastern menu, you are lead to the dining room where you are greeted by your visually impaired host. From then on in you cannot see a thing. Fantastic experience!
Dec 2015 • Family
Who would have thought eating in the dark could be this much fun and be serious dining at the same time!?

Before dinner, guests are given an opportunity to readjust their senses through a simple but effective game. We then selected the "menu from the East" and also picked the house wine.

I was going to this restaurant knowing that is going to be dark but nothing prepared me for the experience... Me and my friends once we spent some time at the reception playing a blind game given from the waiter- a good hint to what follows, we eventually got to a freezing cold and literally pitch black room. Once we all confirmed we are very cold the blind waiter brought the thinnest of scarfs to cover our shoulders defeating the whole aim of the complain to regulate the air condition. The cold was already bringing up a headache and soon I started feeling rather anxious because the absolute dark ( which I was anticipating to get better) remained pitch black and we were getting the smallest of portions of food that made the situation worse. I am vegetarian so I ordered a vegetarian menu which was a fried piece of kind of a bread ( I am not sure because I was shivering at this point) a cold soup of two kinds and a piece of fried courgette I think... The main four plate course( don't be fooled by the four items) I do not even remember what I was eating ( that was half an hour ago....) and then the four pieces of tiny desserts which were more than average. At this point an anxiety attack really kicked in and I could hardly control my self. I nearly dropped down the stairs (because was so dark) and I run out the restaurant once I had to find the locker where I had to leave anything that generates light of any kind ( mobile, matches etc)
Once I run out screaming ( misbehaving rather...) the manager came up to me trying to explain what I already knew. I was under an anxiety attack from the freezing and overwhelmingly dark room and I couldn't hear another word. 
Overall even with the lights on the food was average to basic, cold plates ( misplaced from the blind waiter) and the atmosphere was commercial and marketing based. Dinner was overpriced for what it was and despite the good intentions of the manager, I don't think I will ever go there again.

Thank you for choosing our restaurant and for taking the time to give us feedback on your recent dinner with us. I am really sorry to hear you did not enjoy the dining experience.

There are a few things I like to comment on, since I did not had a proper change to talk to you after dinner.

You told us that we should have warned you that the dining room is going to be complete darkness. Your three friends were aware of the concept, the name of the restaurant is Noir. Dining in the Dark and also the website and reviews on tripadvisor give further information that the dinner is served in darkness and that you cannot see your hand in front of your face. Upon arrival when we explain the menu, let you play with the game, and in the briefing before entering the dining room, we mention multiple times, that there is no light in the dining room.

Guests are more the welcome to step outside the dining room, once they do not feel comfortable.
In case you felt that you could not handle it, do not force yourself to remain seated. We do have some tricks upon our sleeves for situations like yours. Sad enough we could not use those. In the very last resort we could have served you the dinner in the lit part of the restaurant. However you decided to stay and continue to feel uncomfortable, I regret that we could not have assisted you with this earlier.

When we welcomed you back in the lit lounge, which you described rather accurately, you told me and the other guests present, that we should be closed down and that restaurants with dining in the dark would never be allowed in London. Dans Le Noir London has been operating for the last ten years and seems to be rather successful. Our restaurant has been open for 14 months, and permit me to say, it also seems we are rather popular too. We provide guests with unique dining in the dark experiences and employment opportunities for blind and visually impaired staff.

You told us that there is a health and safety concern. Lights in the dining room will automatically switch on in case of an emergency and there are emergency exits to provide safe routes in case of an incident. This is also clearly mentioned on our website.
The staircase is dimly lit, in order protect the eyes from too much light once guests leave the dining room. There is light, it is not dangerous though. There is a handrail that you could have used, as your guide explained.

After dinner we always show our guests the pictures of the menu, as I did with your friends, however you refused to see the pictures. I am not going to give away spoilers, however I can assure you that the you were not served pan-fried bread and courgette.

In regards to your comments, we do not see ourselves as a commercial and marketing based. As I explained your friends in your absence, we are a restaurant that does try our efforts in making sure to provide excellent service and excellent dishes. In essence it is a restaurant. Indeed, there is no light in the dining room, indeed there is blind staff, but we make sure that does not take away anything from the restaurant experience. I regret to hear that that was not how you value us. 
Our social business and restaurant does indeed employ 10 blind and visually impaired staff, for who this is true employment, where we can turn the disadvantage of being blind to become an advantage. In Vietnam, the unemployment rate for the blind community is 94%. Furthermore we have as well five deaf and hearing impaired in our team. Also certain amount of our profit is contributed to help the blind community. 

I am sorry to hear you feel our restaurant is overpriced. Our pricing is comparable to similar restaurants in the area and other restaurants in Saigon and we feel we provide good value for money, especially since many guests comment positively about this. 

As a token of goodwill, I deducted a discount from the check.

We have immediately taken action in regards to the air conditioning and readjusted the setting.

I am completely aware that this concept is not for everyone. We do have a large number of guests who absolutely like what we do, and even return multiple times and introduce their friends and family to enjoy a unique dining experience,
Kind regards,
Germ

reviews.review_text:
Danny S
Brisbane, Australia64 contributions
0
An amazing experience.......
Aug 2015 • Couples
We had heard about this place from friends and decided to give it a go. 
So glad we did. It was truly a great night. 
You are asked to perform some tasks blindfolded before you go in to the dining room so you can practice your spatial awareness. 
You are then led by one the amazing waitstaff in to a completely black room. You cannot see anything. Not even a tiny twinkle of light and your eyes do not adjust. There is literally no light. 
After being led to your table you are asked to feel out for your wine glass and cutlery and the waiter the disappears. 
It was really interesting in that you can hear some of the other diners talking but the dark makes everyone whisper and you have no idea whether the room is small or large or how many other people are sitting around you. 

The food itself is excellent and the wine is matched to the dish. You are encouraged to guess what you are eating to your waiter and We felt quite smug that we did in fact guess every component bar one of the ingredients over 3 courses and I was able to guess the wine type correctly.
 
Because you obviously cannot see your food there is no need for presentation (although you can see the dishes beautifully prepared after the meal, and were some of the most amazing looking dishes I have ever seen. True art). Instead they play with your senses by introducing texture and temperatures for each dish and they are clearly very well thought out for the overall sensory experience. 
Normally at this point I would walk you through the dishes but this would totally spoil YOUR experience. 

After we'd finished our meal we were led back through to the lounge area for a coffee and had the meal and wines shown to us and we were very lucky to have this session with the owner. 
He is a lovely guy and you can tell he has a real passion for what he has created in Noir. He loves what he does and it was clear it wasn't just about the food but about creating a nurturing environment for his staff and a beautiful experience for his diners. 

Incidentally our waiter (and some of the other staff members) was blind. This is clearly the best kind of waiter in this environment and it was awesome to have the opportunity to meet him and I think it's great that someone who might otherwise struggle to find work in a place like HCMC can earn a decent living and receive great hospitality training. 

I cannot recommend this experience enough! 

Perfect for date night or with a small group of friends. Young children might be too loud or overwhelmed by the experience however and would not recommend you take them for you and the other diners!

We take being able to see for granted, this takes everything away from you and makes you rely on other senses. The dining room really is pitch black, you can see nothing and trying to eat in such circumstances is interesting but you soon get used to it. We did notice that not being able to see anything meant that we did talk more! The fun is trying to decipher what you are eating - there are no horrors in there- but there maybe things you have never eaten. When you go through your menu at the end there will be some surprises! This is a real experience and to be fair has made me more understanding of how partially sighted / blind people cope with food.

A New View on life!!
Nov 2015 • Family
"Take care your employees and they will take care of your customers"-Sir Richard Brandson-. This was something, entrepreneurs of Noir, Tu and Germ, have done incredibly. 

The term "the blind leading the blind" has always been viewed as a negative statement however in this case it literally can be used with such GREAT context. Our server for the night Suen(hope i spelt her name right) who was visually impaired, was extremely scrupulous whereby she showed us a great skill of leadership, talent and impeccable service. 

Called and made a booking at 5.20pm and managed to get a reservation for 5.30pm. Went in thinking it was a french restaurant (as i did not read the reviews on trip advisor) however came out with a new view on becoming more patient, more meticulous to the details, more creative and more attentive when the other person is talking. 

It really stops us to think that we humans are so judgmental with the sight of our food and so distracted with our phones at the dinning table but once the lights are off you actually appreciate the simple things in life much more. 

Well done guys on creating value for people will definitely be back next week for my birthday.

"Amazing Dining Experience"
Nov 2015 • Friends
Fabulous Evening. Decided "Noir" was a must do before leaving Australia and it didn't disappoint. 

3 of us went along intrigued at the thought of eating in the dark. 
You arrive and were given a drink to start. You choose alcohol or not. 
You are given two tasks to do blindfolded. This sets the scene for what's to come. 

The staff are so welcoming and friendly. They explain how everything will run so you know what to expect. You choose if you want your menu in either East, West or Vegetarian. (Menu changes seasonally)
We selected East. No phones or watches that light up. Absolutely nothing which creates light allowed into the dining room. 

You are introduced to your waiter who is blind. Then your taken to your table and seated. The room is pitch black. 
And everything is explained. Three courses are brought out. 
This restaurant is 5 Stars. The food is wonderful, delicious, fresh and a true dining experience in every way. 

On completion you are taken to a dimly lit area for your eyes to adjust then out to the lounge bar area. A staff member then goes through what you think you were eating. Pictures are presented and a full meal description explained. 

This is without a doubt one of the most amazing dining experiences I've ever had. 
I highly recommend you visit "Noir" you will not be disappointed. 

Thank you to the amazing staff and the incredible wait staff who made our evening so special.

ElanMorin
Singapore, Singapore70 contributions
0
Tasty
Oct 2015 • Friends
The food was very good. Everything else taken away - the tastes were great and I suppose that's the main bit. Eating in the dark was an incredibly interesting experience, I ended up feel quite weird and wondering if I could actually see (I couldn't, it was pitch black). All very professional, our visually impaired server was great, led us to the table without dying, didnt spill boiling water over us... I'm in awe. I mean, it's like that for him every day, but I'm still thankful. I'd definitely go again.

Suggestions:
- A dark room where you play the games before hand to adjust before you get to your meal (to heighten your senses even more). 
- A layout of the room that you can view after. 
- A video of what you were like when you were in there (but only told about it after the meal).
- Pictures of the dishes as the were presented (the ingredients were interesting but we still wanted to know what the actual dish looked like).
Read more
Written October 31, 2015
Germ D
Dear Elan Morin,
Thank you for your review and it was nice you had dinner at our restaurant.
Dining in the dark does indeed heighten the “other” senses, and as you are deprived of the dominating sense of sight and the dishes that have not been described beforehand, you focus much more on smell, taste and texture. You have discovered the stunning truth that people tend to experience food with their eyes, rather than with their palate.
At Noir. Dining in the Dark we are very proud of our service and it is always a pleasure to know we achieved our goal: providing a unique experience to our guests and meet every guest’s expectations.
They are more than capable indeed. We believe the lack of experience in the service team - none of them had any employment prior to Noir. - is compensated by their passion, enthusiasm and possibility to show our guests how it is to be in a complete dark situation.
Thank you for the suggestions too, however there are still some aspects of the experience we like you to build up ideas with your imagination. It is like reading a book and see the film afterwards, it is always different than what you thought is was.
Glad you liked to come back, we do look forward to welcoming you once more, 
Kind regards,
Germ

Dear WillMac66,
Thank you for visiting us at Noir. Dining in the Dark and for leaving your reaction on the dinner in a review.
I am glad you liked the dinner from service to food and mention it is a good experience. It is indeed a selection of thirteen different dishes, all with different textures, smell and taste and an interesting combination of ingredients. I am pleased to hear you liked it.
I am saddened to hear though, that you think you will not come back and to see your comments on the second restaurant we are about to open with a service team of deaf and hearing impaired. Please do pass by and you will be able to comment after you have actually tried the restaurant, the service and the food. There are many who are rather excited and eager to come. 
Indeed there are many dining options in this city. However there are actually very little restaurants in HCMC and Vietnam in general with employees with special needs, since employment in generally is not created, hence, the unemployment rate of the blind Vietnamese community is 94% and for the deaf around 65 to 70%. We are committed to giving these very talented individuals a chance to work, since they are more than capable of working.
We do have quite a large number of guests who do return to our restaurant, even multiple times. Of course we leave it to you, although I do hope we have the pleasure of welcoming you back again too, as well as come and have dinner at our second restaurant with deaf staff, once we are open, we do look forward to it,
Kind regards,

Frankly, a bit shocked at the favorable reviews. Yes, there is the novelty and experience of eating completely in the dark. As well, there is an honest and true feel-good factor about helping others less fortunate, and walking a mile (i.e. Eating a meal, in their shoes.). Full stop.

As well, this place is insanely overpriced for what you get. Insult to injury is added by the owners showing you gorgeous photos of what you supposedly ate... Frankly, I am highly skeptical. I would much rather have donated my $100USD for dinner for two to charity.
Read more
Written October 16, 2015
Germ D
Dear Sir,
Thank you for choosing Noir. Dining in the Dark and for taking the time to give us feedback on TripAdvisor of your recent dinner at our restaurant.

I have read your comments with attention and really deeply regret that your impression of our menu was disappointing and the food was not suited to your tastes. Noir. Dining in the Dark has been open for a year now and has been rewarded by many positive reviews of guests who indeed are extremely satisfied with the products and services we offer, which is obvious by examining TripAdvisor. 

Our team takes prides in making sure the dishes prepared are to be fully enjoyed by our guests, we are having frequently guests who return, even on the next day to try a second menu. Hence it is truly saddening us that we were not able to make you happy with the dishes at all. 
Dining in the dark does heighten ones senses; the taste, the smell, the texture are more at the foreground. A dinner in the dark is perceived in a different way then it would have been in the light. 
This cycle of the Menu had a Summer theme with many flavours and aromas of fruits. Indeed, we appreciate all constructive comments, even if they are positive or not, as they help us to understand our guests’ tastes and take into consideration for next seasonal menu which is soon launching in one week time. We hope having a chance to welcome you back to try the new Autumn menu. 

Regarding to the pictures of the menu we have showed you are pictures of the true ingredients of the dishes; it is indeed not how the food is served in the dining room, since the pictures focus on the ingredients only. 

Further, we appreciate your valued feedback on our menu prices. Our pricing is comparable to similar restaurants in the area and other restaurants in Saigon and we feel we provide good value for money, especially since many guests comment positively about this. Two times of three-course Menu from the West and a bottle wine and water ended up precisely US$89.83, which we feel is a fair price for a dinner. We regret that this was not your impression and the value we leave to our guests to justify. 

I am glad that you appreciate the concept and the employment of blind and visually impaired staff. I like to emphasise that we are, though, not a charity organisation, nor a novelty dining outlet, but a full working restaurant and we have high expectations of our team, since our guests have high expectations of us. 
At Noir. Dining in the Dark we are passionate about delivering personal service and ensure that guests leave the restaurant more than fully satisfied, taking away only pleasant memories. 

I hope you will give us the opportunity to welcome you back to Noir. Dining in the Dark and regain your confidence with new menu.

I remain at your disposal for any assistance you may require,

Kind regards,
Germ

reviews.review_text:

Amazing Experience!
Apr 2015 • Friends
This was probably the most memorable culinary experience we've ever had. Absolutely amazing from beginning to end. 

When we arrived, we were greeted at the door and seated around a coffee table as we waited for our other friends to arrive. As soon as they did, the owner came around, took our drink orders and introduced us to the two different menus. After we placed our order, he gave us a fun warm up activity to get us ready for the dining experience. 

Before we entered the dining room, we locked up our bags and phones (they were also kind enough to keep my friend's phone on hand as she had a babysitter for her little girl and was worried about any emergencies). The owner introduced us to our guide who slowly and carefully walked us through to our table and seated us with ease. He explained to us where all our utensils were, as well as our glasses of water, which he poured for us when we sat down. It was initially quite stressful, adjusting your eyes to the dark and figuring out where everything was, but after a few minutes, it became much more relaxed. 

Our three courses came quickly, thanks to the wonderful service by our guide, and they were fantastic. Three of us ordered the western menu, and I ordered the eastern menu. It was fun getting to guess what we tasted (which was probably the main point, as opposed to eating a whole portion), especially when it was the same plate. We soon figured out the table setting and my friends even got to taste bits of mine without knocking over any wine glasses! Although it's only three courses, with the amount of small plates, it's surprisingly quite filling. At the end of the dinner, one of the hosts explained the entire menu and what a surprise some of the plates were! My boyfriend, who is a huge foodie, swore he tasted one thing, and it was something else completely.

We would definitely return if we were to visit HCMC as they change the menu every few months. 

Side note: If you have long arms, it's the perfect place to play tricks on your friends ;)

Such A Different Dining Experience.
Jun 2015 • Couples
I read about this restaurant before we visited Ho Chi Minh and decided then it was a must try.
The restaurant is down a lane way by a bakery,it is in a lovely old French style house.
We were warmly greeted when we arrived & given a choice of two drinks.
Then played a little game blindfolded just to set the mood.
We then were introduced to our blind waitress before been led up stairs.
I held on to her shoulders & my husband held on to mine while in total darkness we were taken to our table.You can hear people talking all round but can't see anything.
This in its self is very surreal. Glasses and cutlery are placed in front of you.
Our lovely waitress makes sure we are comfortable with every thing.
We are served different course, in small dishes on a plater and told we start from the top and work around clock wise. Mind and Life Altering Experience!
May 2015 • Couples
I've been meaning to write this review ever sense I left Vietnam a few months ago, but haven't gotten around to it till now... I had such a wonderful time that I promised Germ (owner/host) that I would definitely write a review on TripAdvisor to help repay him for his hospitality and for the the opportunity he gave me to experience such a unique dining adventure.

To be honest, I'm a bit reluctant to share my entire experience because I really feel that everyone should have their own unique experience. I had the fortune of not knowing anything about Noir before stepping in to the foyer/welcoming room of the restaurant (my girlfriend chose the restaurant and she told me it got a lot of good reviews on TripAdvisor, so I said sure, why not). I was a little confused with what was going on and to be honest was a bit nervous because I could tell it was not a normal set up for a restaurant and saw some things that were definitely out of the ordinary. But as the night progressed, I let my guard down and really just took it all in and enjoyed.

I won't go into much detail about the pre or post dinner activities, but I can say that everything is done with purpose to make you appreciate your meal, to appreciate your senses and also most importantly, in my opinion, to appreciate the whole concept of having a business that supports the blind community in a very meaningful and community focused approach.

My girlfriend and I made a connection with our server and learned from him that you can enjoy a meal, the presence of good company and good conversation, regardless if you have the sense of sight in which we have always taken for granted. Learning to eat, drink, LISTEN, even just sense who else was in the room or to hear other conversations was an amazing experience. It's something that I still appreciate months after the experience. I feel that my other 4 senses were and still are more awakened. The food was also quite good, but what I will always remember was the overall experience. It was almost like a course in meditation. 

Keep an open mind, an open heart and enjoy!

Fantastic night out and well worth a visit. Scored lots of points with the wife by booking this and taking her as a surprise. I didn't tell her the twist so she was puzzled about the blind "game" and why they were explaining "how things would work".

The whole experience is great fun and well managed. The owner greeted us and explained how the dinning in the dark would work, we got to do a pre-eating game to test out blind skills.

Guessing the dish was a fun process and it was neat that the waiter wouldn't just tell us -- he gave us clues to help us figure it out, which made each course entertaining, like telling us how the vegetable grew, it's colour, or how many legs the animal had ;)

We had the eastern menu, should have requested the eastern menu with the western dessert (Asian desserts are not that great), meal was a little pricey but for such a interesting experience its well worth it.

After the meal you get de-briefed and taken through what you did actually eat. We were way off on some of our guesses.

Only downside is you can get through the meal quite quickly, and given its a set menu there can be very little time between courses, unlike a traditional restaurant where its talk - order - wait - eat - talk - order - wait - eat - wait etc..

Unique experience
Jul 2015 • Couples
The concept of dining in the dark is not unique. This first started in Switzerland and spreaded across Europe, America and recently Asia. What is so worthwhile about Noir in HCMC is that is relatively cheap (Tourist point of view. But still relatively expensive in the local context). But this does not mean any compromise in the food or experience. 

Staff there are well trained and are knowledgeable about their food. There will be 2 persons directly serving you. One to explain the concept to you and a blind waiter/waitress to lead you into a totally dark room and to wait for your dining. Our experience is that both are really interested in their work. In fact, the first person shared that he was trained in SHATEC, Singapore and was involved in the trials/design of the menus. 

Incidentally, we were told the menu changes every 3 months and we admire the dedication and creativity that the chef and staff needs to put in to ensure the constant novelty in their dishes. Great job and may your recipe stays secret!

The blind waiter who served us was very friendly and helpful too. He shared that he self-learnt Mandarin and was able to communicate with us in fluent Mandarin. We are impressed. 

Hint: the chef there really love to play with your sense of smell, taste and texture. We picked the Western menu but some of the dishes we had tasted oriental. Lots of dishes smell like they contain cheese or peanuts in them, but we are pleasantly surprised by the actual menu. Taste carefully!

Great experience!
Jul 2015 • Couples
Greeted by the most friendly and welcoming wait staff, our first visit to Noir was one to remember. 

My wife and I loved the atmosphere, hidden down an alleyway amidst the chaos of HCM. 

We started with a drink in the lounge, followed by a blindfolded game to help get used to being without sight. Then we were introduced to our lovely waitress, whose name I won't attempt to spell but I believe was pronounced Deyen. My apologies! 

We were seated at our table in complete darkness, our mystery wine and water poured for us and instructions as to where on the table our cutlery and napkins were given to us in well spoken English. My attempts at poor Vietnamese were well accepted by our waitress (thanks for that). 

And so, the food! We chose the Asian menu, with mystery wines. 

Our entree's were served on a wooden board, similar in layout to the sense game from earlier on. Two soups, which were distinct in flavour but complimented each other wonderfully, were followed by three small dishes. Each of these was so tasty and the textures were fantastic. A real treat! 

The main courses were all delicious also, moving from dish to dish was easy by now and my wife and I were having fun, talking about what each dish might be, trying to pick the ingredients and enjoying the wine. 

The dessert course was a highlight, the first dish of Thai black tea icecream was my personal favourite. 

All in all our whole experience at Noir was just fantastic. Great staff, amazing chefs and the concept just works. After our meal the background of the restaurant was explained to us and we had a lovely chat with the manager whilst we had our last drink in the lounge. 

If you come to Vietnam, please come to Noir. Treat yourself.

reviews.review_text:

The most impressive dining experience ever!!
Jun 2015 • Couples
On our first night at Ho Chi Minh City, after checking out this restaurant on tripadvisor, my husband and I decided to go to Noir.
My husband has been to the same dine in the dark sister restaurant in London so he knew what to expect. I however didn't, and was very excited! 

When we arrived we were greeted by a friendly server who explained the concept of the restaurant and what to expect (without giving much away!). We were given a welcome drink (with option of alcoholic or non alcoholic), and three set menu options - western, Vietnamese or vegetarian (which is Vietnamese veggie). Being vegetarian we were glad to go for the veggie menu, but we weren't told what was in it! 

We were then made to play a little game of shapes where we were blindfolded and asked to put the correct shapes into to the corresponding slots. This, we were told would aid us in eating in the dark.

We were asked to place our belongings into a locker so that we couldn't cheat with any light from our phones or even watches! 

We were then introduced to our water, Chiet, a very friendly and well English spoken blind young man, who led us to the dark room very efficiently, up the stairs by having us touch each other's shoulders. 

The actual room was pitch dark!! There were just two little red lights, possibly sensors? 
There were other diners in the room as we heard other voices, but the room itself felt quite spacious and not cramped. We were asked to call out for Chiet when we needed him, and he responded with a friendly call of 'I am coming!' 

We had a lovely three course meal, five starters, four mains and four desserts in bowls arranged on a square tray very similar to the little game we played outside! We were asked to start from the top right and go clockwise. It was quite fun to guess what we were eating! 

After the dinner we were led by Chiet back to the lounge where the server who met with Us Originally came with his iPad to explain and show pictures of what we were served - it was amazing to see how bad we were with our other senses and how much we relied on our sense of sight!

The owner, a European gentleman then came upto us and asked whether we had a good dinner and explained that 97% of blind people in Vietnam were unemployed, but they are actually very intelligent as demonstrated by the servers in the dark rooms. He then proceeded to explain that him and his Vietnamese partner who own this restaurant have had this restaurant opened for 8 months, and are planning to open another restaurant in the upper levels employing deaf and dumb waiters who would respond only with hand signals! 

We very much look forward to coming back and look forward to trying out the new restaurant when it's ready! 

Ten out of ten!

Dinner @ Noir = a very memorable and meaningful experience!
Jun 2015 • Friends
Last night, We ate at Noir and had a very positive experience. it was my first time in a blackout venue like this, and I was intrigued for some time. Several friends had been and we were convinced by word of mouth. It is best to make a reservation. 

We arrived and were offered a mystery welcome drink (option of non-alcoholic was available). We were given a small and simple exercise to get used to the feeling of blindness before we were taken to our table. We looked at the menu, only to see a general but enticing description of each course, without identifying the actual dishes. The menu had the menu items typed in braille which was a very nice touch. There are 3 options: Vietnamese, Western and Vegetarian. Before going to dinner, the host enquired as to whether or not anyone had any allergies, which he noted for the chef. We were introduced to our server before he took us to our table, by following him with hands on the shoulders as we shuffled our way to our table.

The journey up the stairs was dimly lit, but once we entered the dining room, there was absolutely no light (aside from a tiny red light on the aircon). The servers communicated orally, and by the odd tap on the shoulder and guiding hand. The servers knew each of our names and were always within earshot. Service was excellent and careful to help diners know where items are on the table.

The food was very, very good. Each course had 4 or 5 dishes, which we were instructed to eat in sequence from top right, going clockwise. We guessed amongst ourselves about specific ingredients, and in most cases, we were wrong (we insisted on clarification of some items in each course). As a group, we found this funny, since two of us are self-proclaimed foodies and thought we knew everything, and the other two are picky eaters and are not normally adventurous with food. All of us throughly enjoyed our meals. Throughout the meal, we ate many different flavours and combinations, with chicken, beef, fish and duck. 

After dinner, we were escorted back to the lobby. It was quite busy, and we were offered a seat in the garden while we waited. The owner came over to show us an ipad of each dish, and explain what we had eaten for each course. He then offered some insight into the philosophy of the business, the goals to support blind people in Vietnam, and operations of the restaurant.

Portions were not huge, but we were still very, very impressed. They plan to change the menu every 2-3 months, and so I will definitely return for this unique experience. 

Thanks to Nghia, our server and his team, who provided excellent service.

An Experience Not To Be Missed!
May 2015 • Couples
I was wondering why no one told me about this place before, but apparently, Noir just opened a few months ago. Dining in complete darkness certainly sounded interesting and both my wife and I were game!

When we arrived, we were ushered into the waiting lounge, as indicated on their website. We were served a drink and given some very basic training on operating in the dark. We were each given a board with holes of various shapes and were told to fit in the pegs. All while blindfolded of course! I did wonder how that would help us to eat in the dark.

When we were ready, a blind guide took us into the dining room and to our table. My wife placed her hands on the guide's shoulders, I placed mine on my wife's shoulders, and in we go! I got to admit that there was a slight sense of unease walking in complete darkness. We literally could not see anything and we shuffled along at a snail's pace.

Once seated, I felt much more relaxed. I realized that it was not complete darkness as there was a red spot lighting in the room. I suspect that's where the emergency exit is. Anyway, it doesn't matter as it was not bright enough to illuminate anything - I could not see my fingers even when I held my hand just a few inches in front of my face!

Our guide, Mr Triet, was very friendly throughout, keeping up a lively chatter and did his best to allay any concern that we might have. He would always tell us what he was going to do next and always took care to let us know exactly where he was putting the cutlery, the glasses, the plates, etc.

When the food came, I realized why we were asked to play the game at the waiting lounge. Each course did not come in a single plate as we are normally used to. For example, the appetizer consisted of five items, which I shall not reveal as the restaurant would like to keep it a surprise for the diners - we were asked by Mr. Triet to guess what we were eating. 

Anyway, I digress. The five different items were put in 5 separate bowls of different shapes, which were in turn placed on a tray with 5 pegs ....

We both ordered the western menu. Some of the dishes were good, some average. I wouldn't call it fantastic. Mind you, I am not complaining. I think the fact that each course was going to be served in separate bowls and eaten in complete darkness probably put some constraints on the chef's creativity.

As I mentioned in the title of my review, it's the experience that's the main selling point. Mine was certainly different from what I expected prior to the meal. For one thing, it went a lot faster than expected. Our 3-course meal was done within 50 minutes, which was kinda fast, according to the French owner (I am presuming both). I was also worried about spilling on the floor or worse, breaking a plate or two. Fortunately, such accidents rarely happen as people tend to be much more cautious in the dark.

And the social benefit of this restaurant is certainly to be lauded. It's not easy for the visually impaired to find employment. At Noir though, their disadvantage is turned into a distinct advantage! Well done!

It's a little hard to find (down a side-street), but the owner was coming back from an errand as we were looking and very politely pointed us in the right direction. 

Upon entering, we were given 100% of the owners attention as he ran us through the menu (three very simple options, Eastern, Western, or Vegetarian). The rest, he said, was a mystery.

We played a little game with blindfolds on to help us get used things and we were ushered into the dark room.

Our waiter was fantastic. Noir employs locals who are vision impaired. To hear someone speak with so much pride because they have been given a job for the first time in their lives was really quite inspiring. 

Most 'dining in the dark' venues are a bit of a gimmick. The food is ok and the who thing is overpriced. Here, the food is fantastic and value wise it's unbelievable. Three of us had two drinks and a three course menu and we didn't pay more than $30US a head.

I won't go into the menu as I don't want to ruin the surprise, but I was so impressed with this place I was motivated to (finally) sign up to trip adviser and post a review.

What a Fantastic Experience- And the Food Was Great Too!!
May 2015 • Couples
We found this gem through their great tripadvisor reviews and we were not let down one bit. There is so much more to an evening at Noir. than simply having dinner. From the moment that we walked into the lounge area, the dining experience began. We were greeted warmly and offered a complimentary welcome beverage. The owner than came over to discuss the menu with us and take our order. 

Here is where the fun begins... We were then given blindfolds and a puzzle. In order to prepare us for dinner in the dark, we were asked to put on the blindfold and complete the puzzle by putting the various shapes back on the board in the correct position...how fun~!!

After this, we entered the dark room and began our dining experience. We ordered the western menu and wine parings (which I highly recommend if you are a foodie and love wine like we do). Also, it is wise to order the same menu as your date so that you can talk about the flavors and textures that you taste.

Tasting each course created such great conversation as we tried to guess what we were eating. 

Its interesting to notice how human connection changes when your ability to see is removed. In complete darkness, there is no visual distraction to take your focus away from the words of the people that you are communicating with, which makes for a more intimate experience. I even felt a stronger connection with our waitress than typical because I depended on her to lead us through the dark to our table and describe to us what was on the table (wine glass, etc).

THIS WAS SUCH A FUN DINING EXPERIENCE AND A PERFECT DATE NIGHT!

This was a five star experience all around: food, service, and overall experience.

After dinner we chatted with the owners for over an hour and got a sense of the passion behind the restaurant. It is so wonderful that Noir. is providing an opportunity for visually impaired people in Saigon. 

Thank you for the fantastic experience. We loved everything about the evening.

Absolutely amazing experience
Apr 2015
I decided to book dinner here as something special for my husbands 50th birthday celebration. What an experience. I booked from Australia online and always had prompt correspondence from Germ, the owner. The laneway to the restaurant was easy to find. Our taxi driver stopped right out the front. Our complementary welcome drink was very refreshing and taken while we played a small puzzle game while blind folded. The staff service was impeccable. Our hostess who was visually impaired explained how the process worked and we were stunned with her ability. We chose the eastern menu which was a degustation of 13 dishes of beautifully prepared and executed meals designed to make you think about product flavour and texture. After dinner we had a fabulous chat with the owner who went on to further explain his ideas for the concept. Very good value for money for such an amazing experience.

The staff were so helpful in making us feel comfortable in the dining room. It was fun trying to guess what we were eating--for some of the more distinctive flavors and textures it's not that hard; for others, impossible!

As we're backpacking this was a bit of a splurge for us--but so happy we went. Would recommend to anyone as a new, different experience. The model of providing skilled work for blind people in a country where not that many opportunities exist is fantastic.

Excellent food, service and concept
Mar 2015 • Couples
We went to experience blackout dining for the first time in a city that we knew would do an excellent job of preparing a surprise eastern set menu. We were not disappointed. Tham was our host, and was funny and spoke excellent English. He discussed Vietnam and food choices before and after the meal and we really enjoyed his company. The welcome drink was superb (rum with a fermented apricot liqueur). 

After a game with blindfolds to get used to moving things around on the table without our sight we met our amazing waiter Nghai (I have probably spelled his name wrong, and so I apologize!). He was incredibly professional and funny, and did a great job of leading us through the experience. We enjoyed every aspect of it. The best part was that the owners of this restaurant have created an employment opportunity for individuals with vision impairments that may not have had very great employment options otherwise in Vietnam. Nghai really impressed us, and it was a delight to chat with him about what each dish was after we had eaten all the dishes in each course. 

The flower gift at the end of the dinner was beautiful. Very nice touch.

We were both blown away by this establishment, the employees, and the concept, and we hope that other business owners might follow in their footsteps in offering equal opportunity employment options for individuals with disabilities in Vietnam and around the world. In the dining room we are all the same!

Definitely check this place out...the price was very reasonable for what we got (about 1,200,000 VND for two drinks and two set dinner menus).

It's down an alley (well lit!) at the end. Not super hard to find, but you have to search a little!

One of the highlights of two and half weeks in HCMC
Jan 2015 • Family
This is a totally unique experience which should not be missed by any visitors to Saigon! The Noir experience sees diners being led into a pitch black dining room by blind or visually impaired staff who have been trained to impeccably aid and serve their guests.

The restaurant is located down the end of an alley off Hai Ba Trung Street (at no. 178) in a colonial style house. We were greeted on arrival, and seated in a (lighted) lounge area, where we were given an aperitif drink and the menu choices were explained.

There was a choice of two set menus – a 'From the East' menu (480,000++ VND, about $36 AUD) or a 'From the West' one (560,000++ VND, about $42 AUD). Each consisted of starters, main course and desserts, but as far as details of individual dishes go, we were (pardon the pun) kept in the dark.

We chose the West menu and then discussed a couple of dietary restrictions (gluten-free, no fish) with our host Germ, which he was happy to accommodate.

Beyond that, I won't say too much...as part of the magic of this experience is not knowing too much about it in advance. However, I will say we found our sensory experience of the food itself somewhat surprising! I have written more about this and our other HCMC dining experiences at my blog: www.feetonforeignlands.com

Noir Dining in the Dark - New Year, New Inspiration!
Feb 2015 • Friends
Noir - Dining in the Dark has been opened for five months and counting for five times were there, the other experiences I shared my previous reviews. The most touching experience was when I held my birthday in October with a group of 15 people, we were in a private room, the room pitch black, no one could see each other, just feeling and senses, and suddenly someone started playing guitar somewhere in a corner in the darkness, and a high-pitched voice sang Happy Birthday to me from another corner, and then many more were singing from every corner of the room. The sound of the singing was hovering above us, clear as birdsong in the ether sky, like a diva with vocal harmonies, clear like crystal. Only in such circumstances one could feel all what I said.

I have a friend who visited me here Vietnam together with her husband and daughter to celebrate Tet with us. They were staying at the Furama Danang for New Year Eve and they arrived to Saigon on the First Day of New Year, I suggested to have dinner at Noir and reserved a table for eight persons on the 2nd day of Tet, but the Restaurant was full and luckily we got a table but had to wait until 8:15 pm.

Most of family members and friends were very eager and excited to the dinner. Before dinner, I've counted up to surprise my friend and whispered into the daughter’s ear: “can you sing in the dark!?” The daughter has a beautiful voice, she is really talented and could become a professional classical vocalist!
The room was pitch black, totally dark, and the blind waiters direct you to your chair and sit you at the table. The dinner takes place in darkness, we had many conversations, joked a lot and a fun time guessing what the dishes are.

And when the dessert was served, I heard a beautiful clear voice, full of rapture:
“I dreamed a dream in time gone by
When hope was high and life worth living
I dreamed that love would never die
I prayed that God would be forgiving”
She sang the classic song from the famous musical Les Miserables; “I dreamed a Dream”. All our senses were focused on her voice, filled with towering time, time down deep despair. Surely it brought some tears to someone’s eyes.

What makes our life more interesting is the emotions. The emotions you only get through the experience. If you want a new experience, a new inspiration, let's go for Noir Dining in the Dark. I would totally recommend!

It is all about the experience!
Feb 2015 • Couples
Last week we had dinner here, it was really amazing. The concept feels complete, from the beginning where you have to play a little game to the end where the owner (in our case) showed us the different dishes we had. 

The dinner itself is in complete darkness, there is really no light. You can't see a thing, so be prepared. You get a personal (blind) food specialist, who will guide you through the dinner. The food itself is really delicious, but for us it was really hard to guess what we were eating. So the pictures in the end helped us a lot in recognizing what we just had eaten. Probably it will be easier to guess the different dishes if you are a foodie, but still. The diner consist out of approx. 13 small dishes or tapas (5 entrees, 4 main and 4 desert). One small remark here, the dishes are small, we both had enough, but it is not that you get a ton of food. 

The owner is dutch, a real nice guy. It was nice to see someone from the Netherlands running a business in Vietnam. In the end we had a really nice conversation about his business, Vietnam and the Netherlands. For me, this personal attention enhanced the whole experience. 

This restaurant is a little bit more expensive, but it is really worth it. We had an amazing dinner and would recommend it to anyone! 

One tip: A single glass of wine is probably enough for the dinner (a bottle is overkill), choose a soft white one, otherwise the wine will be too dominant for a lot of the dishes.

There are quite a few restaurants around the world that are delivering this concept, however, many of the reviews say they don't rate the food, this is not the case with Noir.
Noir is a beautiful restaurant, the parts that you can see anyway, when you arrive, staff are very welcoming and explain what is going to happen, putting you at ease. Once you have decided which menu you wish to go for and play a game to get you used to using your other senses without sight, they introduce you to your waiter/waitress who takes you to your table, you have to completely trust them, do not be apprehensive, they take really good care of you, it is quite liberating to completely trust them.
The dining area is absolutely pitch black, but don't worry, they do not serve any creepy crawlies. It is incredible how quickly you adapt to dining in this way and so interesting to try to guess what you're eating.
After dining, you are taken back to the lobby and are told what you ate, it is so interesting to find out, in particular there are foods my husband has always stated he doesn't like, but absolutely loved it when he didn't know what it was. The flavours and textures are deceiving.

Sadly, the only thing that would need improvement is the food. We had the Asian menu, beautiful ingredients were used (some I had never tasted before) but some of the dishes were bland and most of them lacked character. It felt like more could have been done for the textures as well. 
And, to be fair, although they nailed it with the textures for the dessert platter, it is a shame that the 4 pieces were all coconut flavoured, or should I say 2 were coconut and 2 tasted nothing. 

So I wouldn't want to spoil the menu since it is part of the concept so, overall, starter : quite nice; main : skillfully cooked, poorly seasoned; dessert : deceiving. 

I've been a chef for nearly 10 years now and had the chance to taste the most amazing food around the world. From street stalls to high end venues, Noir will be remembered for its concept and happily forgotten for it's deceiving menu. Sorry, but this isn't fine dining.

I've been puzzled for a couple weeks now trying to figure what rating Noir deserves, but it certainly does not deserves to be ranked best restaurant in Ho Chi Minh city. 

Being still a young business, blessed with owners that do care about customers feedback, I am sure they will keep improving until every guests eating at Noir leaves dazzled and filled with contempt.

Thank you for the great experience, keep up the good work.

Best dining experience of our lives. Period.
Jan 2015
My boyfriend and I decided we were sick of backpacking and we wanted to have an awesome night out. We are massive foodies and chefs in training, so we have spent a lot of time in Asia exploring the best the culinary scene has to offer. Noir was above and beyond our expectations. 

The atmosphere was perfectly crafted, and the lounge beautifully designed. We loved the welcome drinks, and the (deceptively difficult) sensory games we had to play before entering the dining room. The staff were all smiles, and extremely professional. 

The meal was incredible, easily world class five star standard. All food was harmoniously flavourful, perfectly cooked, and artfully presented (at least it felt like it!). Our server N'gia was charming and extremely attentive. I won't say any more about the meal itself, because the surprise aspect of it was one of the best parts of the experience! What I will say, is it's hardly just eating your dinner in the dark. It's a crazy experience that opens your eyes to how much we rely on sight to know what food tastes like, and you will be surprised on how your senses will betray you! It has completely changed how we taste food, and given us a completely new perspective on flavour.

Finally, we met Tú, one of the owners of the restaurant. We talked to him for quite some time. He is an incredible man with an even more incredible vision for the visually impaired of Vietnam. His, and his parter Germ's dedication to their cause and business is admirable. As we talked to Tú about our travels to Northern Vietnam, he offered to email is suggestions for culinary and miscellaneous activities in the north. We returned home to find he had gone above and beyond with his suggestions, and written extensive ideas for us. We are unbelievably grateful to them for this. If you have the opportunity to talk to Tú, we would most definitely recommend it.

If you are a human, you need to experience this. You WILL love it. Noir is an excellent contribution to the future culinary movement of Southeast Asia. All our recommendations.

Worthy cause. Average Food.
Jan 2015 • Couples
Table booked for 8.30pm. Didn't reach our table until 9.30pm due to a previous larger group turning up late. We were given a welcome drink and then both chose the western menu to see if we could more easily guess the food served to us in the dark. Every experience is personal and although it was certainly unique in that you eat completely in the dark, after the starter I was curious to see if the presentation was as average as the food. Seasoning was lacking, vegetables and fish were over cooked, waiter disappeared for too long, wine got spilt(by me), chair got knocked many times by guests being led in. Menu was uninspired and over priced. I truly wanted to rate this experience more highly but for me the food is the most important aspect in any restaurant and it was just not good enough on the day we visited. Clearly many people disagree and for some people the sensory experience is more important but I just don't think the food was worth the money. I wish the venture good luck so go and judge for yourself.

reviews.review_text:
Zannah J
9 contributions
0
A great experience you should try!
Jan 2015 • Friends
This really is a great experience that you really should try!! 

We really enjoyed the experience in the dining room and our waitress was awesome - she was really friendly and helpful in getting us to adjust to the darkness! We had some fascinating debates in our group as to what we were eating ... It was a great challenge and has helped us think about flavours!

We had such a great experience in the dining room, but because of our experience with the front of house staff I have debated for a while as to how many stars to give this. The European man we were greeted by was a little abrupt and was quick to argue with us about the definition of shellfish ... Which made us a bit uncomfortable. Perhaps there was a cultural disconnect here but we did feel like this gentleman found serving us a hassle (just one person asking not to eat shellfish). This place is popular for a good reason - but that is no reason to treat diners like this.

 Unfortunately when we left the dining room we were left standing for a while and had to ask a couple of times to be told what we had eaten (we knew this was supposed to happen from reviews we had read). They were busy which is understandable - but we then had to ask whether there was somewhere for us to sit down while we waited. We were then shown to an absolutely beautiful upstairs terrace ... And left for another ten minutes. One of us had to go downstairs and ask again to be told what we'd eaten. The Vietnamese staff member who showed us was lovely and apologetic.

Don't let this put you off dining here. Our experience in the dark was awesome and gave us some insight into what it must be like to be blind. ... Just be prepared for the European version of fawlty towers with almost comical abrupt service at the front of house!
Read more
Written January 19, 2015
Germ D
Dear Zannah,

Thank you for spending an interesting evening with us at Noir Dining in the Dark. It was our pleasure to have served you and thank you for your feedback. 
I am glad to hear that you enjoyed the experience as well as the service from the service team in the dining room. Indeed it makes you focus much more on what you are eating.
I have read your other comments with attention and really regret that your first impression of our restaurant was disappointing and the order taking was not what you have hoped for.
At Noir Dining in the Dark we take our guests’ food allergies and dietary restrictions very seriously and I have to apologize for being abrupt and making you feel uncomfortable during taking the order.
You as a guest know your allergy or diet best and I know what the menu is. Since the term seafood or shellfish is often used in broad generic terms, I have to ask questions to really narrow down what we can serve and what we cannot serve to you. I do like to offer the menu as close as possible to as what the chef and his team have designed. If there is a request for allergies and special diets, I do have to ask to make it clear.
Indeed one of you was asking for no shellfish, after asking questions it became clear that she meant including crustacean like prawns, and not just shellfish, like scallop oyster alone. Since there was a prawn in the menu, the kitchen replaced that dish with salmon. 
From our experience in previous situations we have learned to be very specific; for instance when a guest asked to have no onion in the menu. It turned out after the guest cannot eat leek, shallot and onion related vegetables either. We do have to ask, unless you give the information in very clear words.
As you might have noticed it was a night with a rather large number of other guests. I might have been focused on more than just one table. Apologies if that came over as I treated you in a hassle, which was not meant to be like that at all. All of our guests are more than welcome, truly. You have my word on that.
We should have seated you as soon as you came out of the dining room. Again, there were more guests we were attending to. No excuse though. We have taking this feedback and we are working on improving the seating procedure. 
And the comparison with Fawlty Towers, well, lets not talk about the war then.
Thank you for feedback once again and I hope you will give us the opportunity to welcome you back to Noir Dining in the Dark and regain your confidence.
Kind regards,
Germ

Do not be afraid of the dark
Dec 2014 • Family
We turned up as a group of 10 but were 8 finally to dine. It was interesting to see that the reality of eating in total darkness could make the (outwardly) toughest of men panic (though of course they would never admit it). Probably because they were afraid of not being in control. We were asked to choose between western and asian menu but had no idea what would be in them, having eaten both I personally prefer the asian one. Do read the FAQs before you turn up as they would give you a good idea of what to expect and do this because you really want to experience it at least once in your life. A member of my group disobeyed instructions and sneaked in a watch (once again, it's the tough, macho types who tend to be more afraid for some reason) and I found it irritating having to watch a light moving around opposite me throughout the meal. 

Personally, I felt a certain liberty when I first entered the totally dark room (with 4 red dots at the corners), very light. Our guide Vinh spoke excellent English (probably had a very good ear) and was absolutely lovely and steady. We were seated and told to check out our space with our fingers. People tend to talk very loudly in the dark, but it's more important to learn to listen and feel when you cannot see anymore. It wasn't difficult finding your dishes and I preferred to eat with my fingers actually. When you lose your sight, you lose a great part of enjoying your food and I felt that touch helped to compensate a little for that. The food was a little cold most of the time and they were quite tasty but not to die for. You eat in a certain order so that they could come together as a whole, being more or less decomposed so that they could fit into a few containers. The lemongrass soda I had was delicious, by the way, but I didn't enjoy the free cocktails before the meal. As time passed, it became tiring to keep the eyes open, so closing them from time to time could help. As we were leaving the room, Vinh warned us to keep our eyes on the floor so as not to be shocked by the sudden return of light. I felt sorry for him that while we had the chance to see light again at the end of our meal, he would remain in total darkness. 

I enjoyed this experience and would recommend that people try it at least once in their lives. I would have preferred to do it just as a couple or with my own family as I found a large group disrupting, the kids could have benefitted from more philosophical insights during a moment like this when they had no other distractions.

The owners were gentle and kind and they would have to be as people may react weirdly when they face eating in the dark. I would even advise them to work a little more on their tact and anticipate more negative reactions before hand.

Dear Petales,

Thank you for your nice comments about your dining in the dark experience. The team and I enjoyed taking care of you and your friends.
Vinh was very happy to have served you and he was very pleased to hear that you appreciated his services.
We have indeed noticed that some extrovert people can become quite timid and at the other hand introvert people can really open up in the dark.
It in the dark the smallest light is already very noticeable. That is why - besides obvious light emitting devises, as phones or lighter - we also ask guests to place their watches in the lockers. Besides being annoying for you, it can indeed also spoil the experience for other diners in the room.
It is good to hear that you liked the drink, and a pity we could not please you with the welcome drink. We have received quite a few good comments about the welcome drink.

Indeed eating in the dark in the dark is an experience. Part of the concept is that we do not let our guests know what we are serving. It is a given that people tend to talk louder in the dark, at the other hand, ones hearing is sharper since your sense of sight is taken away. There is no need for that, since you are not further away from each other than in a regular dining situation, and again since your sense of hearing is sharper in the dark. That is also why we brief guests about this before entering the dining room. 
We had some measure taken already and implemented sound reducing fabrics in the rooms. This was obviously not enough, hence I am pleased to tell you that we installed over the last two days upgraded sound reducing foam on ceilings and walls.

reviews.review_text:
Tuan T
Rockville, Maryland279 contributions
0
Of all the restaurants, in all the towns, in all the world, do walk into this one
Dec 2014 • Friends
Saigon. A big grimy city, filled with tough guys, narrow alleys, cheap bars, and greasy hash houses. I was hungry. Real hungry. So hungry I could taste it. There was a restaurant out there. And it was my job to find it. TripAdvisor.com was like a sewer. And I was going to lift the manhole cover. The big numero uno is this place called Noir. Noir. What kind of name is that for a grub joint? After reading a few reviews, the pieces of the puzzle were falling into place. Are you thinking what I’m thinking? 

Sorry about that. I just couldn’t help myself. Anyway, after reading the reviews and the FAQ on Noir’s website, I called to make reservations. It was a great experience. And like all experiences, I prefer it to be spoiler free, so I’ll refrain from detailed play-by-play recount of our dinner. However, whenever I tell my friends about it, they all have the same questions. So here are some answers.

Yes, you should go, most definitely. Yes, it was pitch black and even with some adjustment time, you still cannot see a thing. Yes, it was challenging but you will be surprised how fast you adapt and find ways to make it work for you. Yes, there was silverware on the table, although a few in our group occasionally switched to using their fingers. Yes, the staff took great care of us from seating us, serving us, and removing our plates when done. In fact, Nghia, our server, was super attentive, giving us specific instructions every step of the way. Yes, Nghia spoke English. Yes, Nghia is blind. No, Tuan, the chef is not blind. Yes, the food was delicious. No, they didn’t serve you anything disgusting; this is fine dining, not a prank TV show. No, we did not leave hungry. And, lastly, I don’t know if we made a mess or not; we couldn’t see anything, remember? At least, there was no spillage on our clothes. 

After the meal, we were lead out to the lit part of the complex and Germ, the owner, sat down with us and showed us on his iPad what we just ate. There were some surprises and a few confirmations too. Germ was very gracious and answered all of our questions regarding the concept of the restaurant, his experiences in the business, putting together the restaurant, his staff and their training.

I’d say go ahead and call to make your reservations. It is a fun experience, and pardon the expression, a real eye-opener. And, the food is very good! 

There are eight thousands grub joints in this city. This has been one of them. And now that I have cracked this case, I hope my next one involves a blonde, because blondes always mean trouble, and trouble is my middle name.

A sensory journey not to be missed
Dec 2014 • Business
Noir is an experience not to be missed, not only due to the sheer brilliance and sensory enlightenment of dining in the dark, but also for the food itself. 

While the concept itself is not new, the restaurant has already reached #1 on the must do restaurants for Ho Chi Minh City in only 8 weeks, and after being there it is not hard to understand why. From the moment we entered the alleyway where Noir can be found, a security guard with a flashing torch helped to direct us, at at the door we were greeted by a friendly waitress. 

The young Dutch owner himself also took the time to welcome us, provide an overview of the menu and explain the experience. The menu, written both in English and Braille, is simply a choice between East and West cuisine. The rest you must discover yourself during the dining experience. I had prepared myself to eat in the dark, but had always expected a trickle of light would be there to help us. Yet before you enter, all light emitting devices are surrender, watch, phone etc and put in a safety locker. You are then greeted and guided by your host to the dining room, which is in fact pitch black. As you work your way through the three courses, each with four or five small dishes, the guessing game begins. Is that pea or potato? What meat is that. You learn to use distance and two hands to poor your water, to tilt your head when you want to direct something to your host. What makes this so special, is that those who are servicing you - and the service is impeccable - are all blind or vision impaired themselves. So as you work your way through the food you get an understanding of what they must go through every day. The food itself would stand up on its own, even in the light. And at the end of the meal, the owner again greets you with ipad in hand to explain what you in act just ate. 

It was a wonderful end to our holiday here, and if every visiting again would defiantly come back to.

Thank you for a great experience.

Noir Dining in the Dark - SENSATIONAL
Nov 2014 • Friends
One word for you, Noir. Dining in the Dark - Saigon : SENSATIONAL.

I remember the very memorable line in my first ever Scuba Diving lession: Once you breathe under water, you'll never forget the first time you ever Scuba Dive.
I believe this should also be changed to: Once you Dine-in-the-Dark, you'll never forget your very first impression on the experience.

Absolutely Five star service And if people in the F&B industry knows me very well, I HARDLY give 5 stars to any outlets. 

I was here with my friend; she was the one who introduced me actually. I was greeted warmly by one of the owners, while I was still in awe of the Contemporary Indochine design. They say the First Impression is the Reception area, well, you surely got me on the hook.

After my friend arrived, we were treated a complimentary cocktail, Notice: both Alcohol & Non-Alcohol. While waiting, I got to play 2 games as a Teaser of the dinner ahead. I had to cover my eyes up with sleep mask, used my both hands only and my touch. Try yourself, friends 

Before we enter the dining room, we were introduced to our server for the night (he was sight-impaired) and how we should move while we're in the room. Already feel excited?? Wait.

Each of us had to put our hands on the people's shoulder in front of us and follow the server into the room. The whole room was PITCH BLACK. We could only hear our voices and others from now on (now I had to confess, my watch has a glowing effect :)) but not enough to know what or who is in the room, however this glowing watch was not my intention though). 
We talked a lot in the room. You should notice: if you're scared of darkness, make sure you come with someone who's confident enough to calm you. I was perfectly fine and even enjoyed the meal. Why?

They said when you have one sense impaired, the others heightened.
I used all my touch, smell, taste, even sound, to guess what was in the dishes. Yes, the dishes come at a surprise with no previous introduction.

Overall, I'm so happy and amazed at such a wonderful & unforgettable F&B experience. I've only heard and seen this type of outlet in the US or movies, but never expect it in my country.

So guys, come and support, for your own enjoyment as well as supporting the restaurant and students from sight-impaired school. They are well-groomed, well-behaved and well-performed.

Wonderful experience for both meaning of dining with your senses and social responsibility. Strongly recommend to try!
Nov 2014 • Couples
This is my first time with Tripadvisor’s review as I would like to share my most special experience in my life. It’s all about Dining in the Dark experience in Saigon.

Upon arrival I was welcomed by a hostess and in the lounge I was offered a free welcome drink, you have a choice of non-alcoholic or alcoholic, I selected Nuoc mo – Apricot alcoholic Cocktail, very creative and good drink. The hostess explained me all the rules like that we can't bring inside any gadgets that emit lights. Those had be deposited inside a secure locker, just to make sure that no one spoils the experience. My partner & I surrendered our phones and enjoyed the meal with dining companions, no facebook or check-in or so. Actually it was liberating to be without your phone for a while.

The adventure began the moment we stepped into the darkness. I was so excited because it's completely dark inside. It's pitch black, all I could hear was people chatting, giggling and sounds of cutleries onto bowl/plates, the moment I got in there, I totally could not see anything, not even my hand!!! 

We were told to sit down and then our guide – Mr. Triet started pouring our wine. One by one, the food was served and it was a interesting experience because we didn't know what exactly we were eating, our guide he is extremely smart, he just give us a hint and keep on guessing. 
I wouldn't reveal what food as it was a part of experience, they have three mystery menus: from the East & from the West and Vegan set menu but I can guarantee you it is not some junkie food. The food was very tasty, it's perhaps because we couldn't see anything at all and that's why our taste buds were particularly sensitive. Later when we were in the Lounge, the manager presented us photos and explained the menu. The dishes were fantastically presented, not as we imagined. 

After the dinner, it was revealed that the all the serving waiters and waitress in the dining room are visually impaired or blind. I was surprised and I respect them so much because they knew the way better than us, I also noticed Noir also would like to share part of their profit to create a fund for eyes operation for disadvantage visually impaired children. How touching and appreciate the ideas of this Restaurant. 

This is indeed very wonderful experience for both meaning of dining with your senses and social responsibility. Strongly recommend to try!

A venue for team building
Oct 2014 • Business
I have had dinner in this restaurant twice, the first time with my partner, where I found it a little tensed as I have tried my best to see what were around me, of course, I have not seen anything as it was totally dark, we have taken our food like blind people. My partner was crying :-), we understand more the lives of blind people. Xuan was serving our table at that night, she was one of the best staff there, explained us, helped us to enjoy our food.

I decided to organize my birthday party there with my close friends and colleagues from my office in Ho Chi Minh city. Before the dinner, we were sitting at the lounge, have been trained with some games while our eyes were blinded, that was interesting. The special cocktails Germ made for us were with rum and local dried fruits, taste wonderful. We spent some times to take some photos in front of the restaurant before getting into the dining room. We were group of 12 people then we took the whole dining room upstairs. Each of the staff, they are all blind, takes each three of us upstairs, the way to the room darker as to make our eyes get use to the new dining room experience: the dark. All of the staff here were very well trained, I know, it took a long time to train them. The staff is very professional, they show us where to sit, what were on the table, they serve wine red and white, mineral water without any mistakes. Excellent. Of course, we did not know who is front of us so we take time to introduce each other, who sitting on the right, on the left, in front of us. This was my second time so I already knew what would make me more comfortable, that I don't try to see anything but only feel things. We have talked, we have singed and make fun, in the dark!

And the restaurant and staff has made me really touched: when we finished the main course: we heard one melody by the flute with the song Happy Birthday on the right of me, and then continued by a guitar from the left of me, then from the 4 corners, all staff were singing Happy Birthday to me. It is really touching to me. Then we all sang the song. 

We cut the birthday cake at the terrace, where we drank champaign, tea and cakes. My friends and colleagues have continued talking about what they felt in the dining room. This was a wonderful experience and it is precious to us, it totally changed our behavior to life.

Thanks again Tu, Germ, Vinh, Duyen, Tan, My for having made my birthday celebration party a memorable one. See you soon!

reviews.review_text:
